findings.finding_text: Menu pricing is locked in 24 months prior to the event (double CD's 12-month standard), and any F&B shortfall is billed at 100% of the difference rather than CD's 35% fallback. With a $185,000 minimum, a total shortfall would cost Group the full $185,000 rather than roughly $64,750 under CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimums should lock in pricing no earlier than 12 months before the event, and shortfalls should be billed at 35% of the gap, not dollar-for-dollar.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will not be established earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the $185,000.00 minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall provide Group with menus and pricing no later than twenty-four (24) months prior to the Event dates
findings.exposure_basis: Full F&B minimum of $185,000 billed at 100% shortfall vs. 35% under CD standard (potential exposure difference of ~$120,250 in a full-shortfall scenario).

findings.finding_text: Contract mandates exclusive use of Hotel-appointed vendors and imposes a $2,500 surcharge per unauthorized outside vendor engagement, contrary to CD's position that Group should be free to use outside vendors at no additional fee.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use the outside vendor of its choice at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours. Hotel's in-house vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group's use of any outside vendor in violation of this requirement shall incur a surcharge of $2,500.00 for each such engagement.
findings.exposure_basis: Flat surcharge per unauthorized outside vendor engagement.

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night (not cumulatively) with a 90% threshold (higher than CD's 70%), damages assessed at 100% of room rate (not 70%), no relief for hotel sell-out nights unless 100% occupancy hotel-wide, occupancy records deemed final/binding with no audit rights, and no F&B offset. This is a severe departure from CD's standard across nearly every element.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition should be cumulative across the block, trigger only below 70% pickup, be calculated using a formula-based approach at 70% of room rate, allow 95%+ occupancy nights full credit, and provide audit rights.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate. For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment. At Group's request, Hotel will provide supporting occupancy records to verify the calculation, and excess F&B revenue will offset attrition damages and vice versa.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall be liable for attrition damages at the rate of one hundred percent (100%) of the nightly room rate for each unoccupied room within the block.
findings.exposure_basis: Full block of 680 room nights (170x4) at $289 = $196,520 if fully vacant; but with 90% threshold and 100% rate, a shortfall to e.g. 50% occupancy (340 room nights unsold across 4 nights) would yield approximately $98,260 in one scenario. Using worst-case full-block value at $289/night x 680 room nights = $196,520 as base illustrative exposure; however full contract value at 100% liability for entire block across 4 nights totals $196,520. Adjusted to reflect total contracted room-night value exposed to 100%-rate attrition penalty.

findings.finding_text: Liquidated damages are calculated against gross room revenue (not room profit at 70%), on a sliding scale up to 100%, with no floor/liability-free window (even day-one cancellation post-signature incurs 25%), no mitigation/resale credit, and no rebate credit for rebooking. This substantially exceeds CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a sliding scale against room profit (70% of rate), hotel must mitigate via resale and credit proceeds, credit for rebooking within a year, no liability more than 12 months out, no punitive damages.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit — defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate — on a sliding scale, with no liability for cancellation more than twelve (12) months prior to arrival. Hotel will undertake reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and credit those revenues against the cancellation fee. Should Group rebook the Hotel within one (1) year, Hotel will credit 100% of the rebooking room revenue toward damages owed.
findings.quoted_text: liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned by the Hotel for all guest rooms for all nights within the event period
findings.exposure_basis: Full block value: 680 total room nights x $289 = $196,520 at 100% liquidated damages rate for late cancellation, with no mitigation credit.

findings.finding_text: Force majeure is narrowly limited to events causing physical impossibility (war, terrorism, earthquakes, floods) and explicitly excludes government travel restrictions/advisories, pandemics/epidemics, and attendee safety concerns — directly contrary to CD's standard. Deposits are also expressly non-refundable upon force majeure.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should cover illegality, impossibility, or commercial impracticability, explicitly including government travel restrictions, epidemics/pandemics, and attendee safety concerns, with prompt refund of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability if performance is rendered illegal, impossible, or commercially impracticable due to acts of God, war, government regulation or advisory, disaster, strikes, civil disorder, curtailment of transportation, epidemic or pandemic, or circumstances making it unsafe or imprudent for attendees to travel to or assemble at the Hotel. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) business days of notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: government-issued travel restrictions, travel advisories, or governmental directives limiting group gatherings or travel, regardless of the reason such restrictions or advisories are issued; epidemics, pandemics, or declarations of public health emergency, including any government responses thereto; or concerns among Group members regarding attendee safety, willingness to travel, or health considerations

findings.finding_text: Cutoff date is set at 45 days prior to arrival (outside CD's 21-30 day standard), and reservations after cutoff are handled exclusively at rack rate rather than group rate subject to availability.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff date should be no earlier than 21-30 days prior to arrival, with post-cutoff reservations still available at group rate subject to availability.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to the group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, the Hotel will continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations for rooms within the block committed for the National Association of Coastal Engineers event shall be accepted by the Hotel only when received on or before forty-five (45) days prior to the arrival date

findings.finding_text: Relocation clause shifts all costs (alternate lodging, taxes, resort fees, transportation) to the displaced guest, provides no upgrade/amenity on return, and excludes relocated nights from pickup/commission credit — directly contrary to CD's standard requiring hotel-paid relocation and no attrition impact.
findings.cd_standard: If the hotel walks a guest, it should pay for comparable/better accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, upgrade/amenity on return, and credit the night toward Group's pickup with no attrition liability.
findings.proposed_language: If the Hotel is unable to accommodate a guest with a confirmed reservation, Hotel will, at its own expense, provide comparable or better accommodations, round-trip transportation, message forwarding, and an upgrade/welcome amenity upon return. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall make a reasonable effort to secure alternative lodging at the guest's sole expense and cost

findings.finding_text: Hotel reserves right to impose new fees at any time, even after signature and even if undisclosed prior to signing, and Group waives any objection. Includes a $35/night resort fee applied even to complimentary rooms.
findings.cd_standard: All mandatory fees must be disclosed in writing prior to signature; any undisclosed charge is waived outright.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges associated with the Event, including resort fees, surcharges, and service charges. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel reserves the right to impose additional fees, surcharges, and service charges upon Group at any time, including without limitation after the execution of this Agreement.
findings.exposure_basis: $35/night resort fee x 340 peak room-block nights x 2 nights avg (illustrative); calculable base: 680 total contracted room nights x $35 = $23,800 if applied to full block across event.

findings.finding_text: Complimentary room ratio is 1:75 (worse than CD's 1:40 standard), is explicitly non-binding/discretionary ('guideline only'), can be reduced or withdrawn at any time, and is entirely forfeited if the block is not 100% met — despite Group still owing full attrition damages elsewhere.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned on a clear cumulative formula (1 per 40 room nights) and not forfeited due to attrition already being penalized elsewhere.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block, regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met.
findings.quoted_text: The complimentary room ratio of seventy-five (75) stated above is a guideline only and does not create an entitlement in Group.

findings.finding_text: Assignment requires Hotel's sole and absolute discretion consent with no reasonableness standard, and no carve-out for assignment to a successor association management company.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign to a successor management company/affiliate without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations and the event program remains substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment is entirely within Hotel's sole discretion and may be withheld in Hotel's absolute discretion for any reason whatsoever, or for no reason at all.

findings.finding_text: Hotel disclaims any obligation to disclose renovation plans, may commence work without notice, and Group has no termination or remedy rights even if the work materially interferes with the event.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should represent no current renovation plans and commit to 30 days' notice of confirmed plans, with Group able to terminate without liability if it interferes.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation affecting Group's space. If Hotel later confirms such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days describing scope, schedule, impact, and mitigation plan. If Group determines the work will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate without liability.
findings.quoted_text: such work shall not constitute grounds for the Group to terminate this Agreement, to claim damages or loss of value, to demand a rate reduction or credit, or to pursue any other remedy or relief against the Hotel

findings.finding_text: Group waives any right to dispute invoiced charges after receipt, invoices deemed final/binding, no defined dispute window (only referenced as 'timeframe specified in master account documentation'), finance charge of 1.5%/month applies (above CD's 1% cap) with no true dispute right, and prepayment amount is entirely at Hotel's discretion with no defined percentage cap.
findings.cd_standard: Master account payable upon invoice with a real dispute window before finance charges apply, finance charge capped at 1% per month, and prepayment as a defined percentage if credit not approved.
findings.proposed_language: Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues. Finance charges will not exceed one percent (1.0%) per month on unpaid, undisputed balances. If credit is not approved, prepayment will be limited to a defined percentage of estimated charges.
findings.quoted_text: the Group waives any right to dispute or withhold payment of billed amounts after receipt of an invoice from the Hotel

findings.finding_text: Group has no right to weekly pickup reports, no audit rights whatsoever (explicitly waived), and post-event report is deemed final/binding unless objections raised within 30 days — with occupancy records under the attrition clause also declared unreviewable.
findings.cd_standard: Group should receive weekly pickup reports, a full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost audit right comparing guest lists.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting a set number of days prior to cutoff, and a full post-event report within thirty (30) days of departure. At Group's request, Hotel will conduct a room block audit at no cost, comparing Hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have no right to audit, inspect, or verify the Hotel's room block records, reservation systems, or internal accounting related to Group's event, and Group waives any audit rights it might otherwise possess

findings.finding_text: Indemnification is one-sided: Group must indemnify Hotel even for Hotel's own ordinary negligence (carve-out only for gross negligence/willful misconduct), while Hotel expressly disclaims any indemnification obligation to Group.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence or willful misconduct; Group should never indemnify Hotel for Hotel's own negligence.
findings.proposed_language: Each party will indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party against claims arising out of the indemnifying party's own negligence or willful misconduct. Neither party indemnifies the other for that other party's own negligence.
findings.quoted_text: This indemnification obligation shall extend to claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence in its provision of services or maintenance of premises

findings.finding_text: The $25,000 security deposit may be applied against attrition, F&B shortfalls, cancellation penalties, and other unrelated charges (commingled use expressly permitted), refund window is 90 days (not 30), and deposit is held in Hotel's general operating account without segregation.
findings.cd_standard: Deposit should be reasonable, refundable within 30 days absent documented damage, and not commingled with or offset against attrition/F&B minimums.
findings.proposed_language: The security deposit will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the event's conclusion unless Hotel provides an itemized accounting of specific documented damage. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may apply the security deposit, or such portion thereof as necessary, against any attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damages to the Hotel's premises, incidental costs, outstanding room charges, service failures, cancellation penalties, or any other sum
findings.exposure_basis: Full security deposit amount at risk of being applied to unrelated charges without segregation or prompt refund.

findings.finding_text: Group's termination for cause is severely constrained: even material uncured breach by Hotel does not relieve Group of damages liability (including lost profit/consequential loss owed to Hotel), and all terminations by Group for any reason are deemed cancellations subject to the full liquidated damages scale, contrary to CD's standard that termination for cause should carry no liability.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should let Group walk away with no liability and prompt refund, separate from the cancellation damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits within five (5) business days, upon force majeure, labor dispute, material change in ownership/brand, or interfering renovation. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: any and all termination by Group shall be deemed and treated as a cancellation subject to the cancellation damages scale set forth in this Agreement

findings.finding_text: Notice of brand/ownership/management change is only 'commercially reasonable efforts' with a 90-day window and Group has only 10 days (not 30) to elect termination; bankruptcy/foreclosure/receivership explicitly excluded from any notice or termination right.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should notify Group within 30 days of a change, and Group should be able to terminate within 30 days of notice, including for bankruptcy/foreclosure.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days. Group may terminate without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice.
findings.quoted_text: the Group acknowledges that the Hotel may be subject to bankruptcy, foreclosure, receivership, or other insolvency proceedings, and that such events shall not trigger any notice requirement, termination right, or remedy available to the Group

findings.finding_text: Named storm clause exists but requires cancellation notice within an unusually tight 24-hour window of NWS warning issuance (or the right expires), and Group forfeits its entire deposit upon invoking the right, with no refund unless the event is rescheduled.
findings.cd_standard: Named storm clauses should allow cancellation without liability upon a storm threat within a reasonable window, without requiring forfeiture of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability, including full refund of deposits, upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice.
findings.quoted_text: Should Group invoke the named storm cancellation right, Group shall forfeit the deposit paid to the Hotel, which shall be retained by the Hotel as partial compensation
findings.exposure_basis: Full $25,000 security deposit forfeited upon invoking named storm cancellation right.

findings.finding_text: Contract explicitly authorizes Hotel to use attendee data for its own marketing purposes and to share it with affiliates/third-party marketers without further consent, contrary to CD's standard that attendee data should be used only for reservation fulfillment.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list/attendee data should be used solely for reservation fulfillment, not Hotel marketing or third-party disclosure without consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.
findings.quoted_text: Group acknowledges that the Hotel may utilize such attendee data for the Hotel's own marketing, promotional, and business development purposes, including but not limited to direct mail, email marketing, targeted advertising, and future event solicitation

findings.finding_text: Hotel disclaims all ADA warranties, places all responsibility (including cost) for accessibility assessment and auxiliary aids on Group regardless of location within the Hotel (including public/common areas), contrary to CD's standard dividing responsibility.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should warrant ADA compliance of common areas/guest rooms/function space, with Group funding aids only in function space and Hotel funding aids in guest rooms/common areas.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the ADA. Group is responsible for auxiliary aids needed in function space; Hotel is responsible for auxiliary aids required in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the accessibility of its facilities under the Americans with Disabilities Act

findings.finding_text: Governing law/venue is Maryland (Hotel's location, not Group's), Hotel is entitled to punitive damages, and the 'prevailing party' (deemed to be Hotel upon any material relief) recovers full attorney's fees, contrary to CD's standard of mutual fee responsibility and no punitive damages.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law/venue should be Group's location, no punitive damages, each party bears own attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed under the laws of the state where Group is located, with disputes resolved in courts in Group's city. Any award will be limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not apply. Each party will bear its own attorney's fees.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall be entitled to recover, in addition to all other remedies available at law or in equity and in addition to any actual damages awarded, an award of punitive damages to the extent permitted by applicable law

findings.finding_text: Hotel has no obligation to disclose CBA expiration dates or labor disputes, and Group has no cancellation right whatsoever for labor disputes/strikes affecting the Hotel, contrary to CD's standard permitting cancellation without liability within 90 days of the event.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should give advance notice of CBA expirations and labor disputes; Group should be able to cancel without liability if a strike/lockout arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will notify Group in writing within ten (10) working days of becoming aware of any labor dispute. If, within ninety (90) days of the Event, a strike, lockout, or expired labor contract occurs, Group may cancel without liability.
findings.quoted_text: the Group shall have no right to cancel this Agreement based upon the occurrence or threatened occurrence of any such labor-related event

findings.finding_text: Hotel retains absolute right to sell rooms below Group's rate with no obligation to adjust, and even when it does elect to adjust, no retroactive adjustment applies to already-confirmed reservations, and any adjusted rate is stripped of commission/pickup credit — contrary to CD's standard of automatic parity adjustment, including retroactively, without losing commission credit.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should guarantee no lower public rate than Group's rate; if violated, Group's rate should adjust (including retroactively) without losing commission or pickup credit.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted rate during the Event dates (except qualified rates). If violated, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match, and such rooms remain fully commissionable and creditable toward pickup.
findings.quoted_text: No retroactive adjustment to Group's rate shall apply to reservations already confirmed prior to the date on which the lower rate is identified.

findings.finding_text: Gratuity and service charge are conflated/used interchangeably with no distinction, combined at 24% with the Hotel retaining full discretion over allocation (may keep entirely as revenue), contrary to CD's standard requiring gratuity be fully distributed to staff and any separate service charge disclosed as such.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined; gratuity fully distributed to staff; service charge disclosed as hotel revenue.
findings.proposed_language: Any gratuity charged to Group's account will be fully distributed to staff working the Event. Any separate service charge is not distributed as a tip and is retained by Hotel; both charges and their percentages will be disclosed to Group in writing.
findings.quoted_text: the terms 'gratuity' and 'service charge' shall be used interchangeably throughout this Agreement and are not separately defined
findings.exposure_basis: 24% service charge/gratuity applied to $185,000 F&B minimum plus applicable room charges; illustrative calculation on F&B minimum alone: $185,000 x 24% = $44,400 in fees with no assured staff distribution.

findings.finding_text: Hotel explicitly disclaims any duty to resell canceled/attrition rooms, retains 100% of any resale revenue without crediting Group, and Group waives any right to audit or challenge resale efforts — the opposite of CD's mitigation standard.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should have an affirmative duty to attempt resale of canceled rooms and credit proceeds against damages owed, with records available to Group.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues, less substantiated transaction costs, against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group. Records documenting this mitigation effort will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall have no obligation to attempt to resell such released inventory or function space, nor shall the Hotel be required to undertake any specific actions, marketing efforts, or promotional activities directed toward filling released space

analysis.document_notes: This is a fully drafted, executable Group Sales Agreement (unsigned) between Harborview Grand Hotel and National Association of Coastal Engineers for April 12-16, 2027. The document is complete and legible with no structural issues. Notably, the contract is heavily one-sided in favor of the Hotel across nearly every clause reviewed — attrition, cancellation, F&B minimums, indemnification, audit rights, force majeure, labor disputes, ADA, governing law, and vendor exclusivity all deviate substantially and consistently from CD's standard positions, several containing explicit waiver language stripping Group of audit, dispute, and remedy rights. This pattern across so many clauses (rather than isolated deviations) should be flagged to the client as a broader risk profile of the document, not just individual clause issues. Several exposure calculations are illustrative estimates built from the room rates, block size, and F&B minimum figures stated in the contract; where the contract's damage formulas are conditional on unknown future occupancy/consumption shortfalls, only the maximum calculable figures (e.g., full block value, full F&B minimum, full deposit) are given, and actual exposure will depend on actual event performance."

findings.finding_text: Section 1 sets the F&B minimum at $48,000, but Section 9 sets a conflicting F&B minimum of $40,000 for the same event dates, with pricing lock and shortfall terms attached only to the $40,000 figure. Beyond the internal inconsistency, the shortfall penalty in Section 9 is dollar-for-dollar (100% of the shortfall) PLUS an additional 35% surcharge on top of that shortfall, which is far worse than CD's standard of paying only 35% of the shortfall gap. This is a significant, stacked exposure: full shortfall plus a 35% penalty rate on top.
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimum shortfalls should be billed at 35% of the gap between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full difference, and menu pricing should not be locked more than 12 months before the event.
findings.proposed_language: Group agrees to a single, unambiguous food and beverage minimum of $[X] (exclusive of service charge and tax), superseding any other stated minimum in this Agreement. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall and not any additional surcharge on top of the shortfall. Menu prices will not be established earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event.
findings.quoted_text: The shortfall rate shall apply to any shortfall amount, assessed at thirty-five percent (35%) in addition to the base shortfall.
findings.exposure_basis: If actual F&B revenue is $0, Group would owe the full $40,000 shortfall plus 35% of $40,000 ($14,000) = $54,000, versus CD standard of 35% of $40,000 = $14,000 — a swing of roughly $40,000 in exposure.

findings.finding_text: Attrition is cumulative and includes 95% single-night credit and audit rights, matching most of CD's standard. However, the liability threshold is set at 75% pickup (not CD's 70%) and damages are calculated at 70% of room rate for unoccupied rooms below that higher threshold — meaning the group is liable for shortfall sooner (at 75% pickup) than CD's preferred 70% floor.
findings.cd_standard: Liability should trigger only if pickup falls below 70% of block, with damages at 70% of the confirmed group rate.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability will be triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block, calculated cumulatively. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate (plus applicable tax).
findings.quoted_text: Should Group fail to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of committed rooms, Group shall pay the Hotel liquidated damages equal to the room rate applicable to the unoccupied rooms, multiplied by seventy percent (70%), for each night the threshold is not met.
findings.exposure_basis: Difference between 70% and 75% threshold on 90-room block = 4.5 rooms x 4 nights x $199/night x 70% damages rate ≈ $3,134.25 of additional exposure created by the higher 75% trigger versus CD's 70% standard.

findings.finding_text: The cancellation clause's narrative text states cancellation more than 12 months before arrival carries no liability, 6-12 months is 50%, and within 6 months is 100% — but the accompanying table imposes a five-tier sliding scale starting at 18% for cancellations 365+ days out (i.e., liability even for cancellations more than a year in advance) rising to 70% inside 30 days. The table conflicts directly with the narrative text and is worse than CD's standard, which calls for zero liability more than 12 months out and calculates against room profit (70% of rate), not gross liquidated damages as stated in the table's basis.
findings.cd_standard: No liability for cancellation more than 12 months prior to arrival; sliding scale based on room profit (70% of group rate), not gross revenue.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit — defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate — on a sliding scale based on days prior to arrival, with no liability whatsoever for cancellation more than twelve (12) months prior to arrival. The table in Section 4 should be revised to eliminate the 18% charge for cancellations 365+ days prior to arrival and to align percentages and terminology with the narrative text of this clause.
findings.quoted_text: 365 days or more prior to arrival  | 18%

findings.finding_text: Force majeure clause substantially matches CD's standard, including pandemic/epidemic and travel-advisory language, and prompt refund of deposits within 30 days. This is a positive/compliant clause; flagged for completeness only.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should cover illegality, impossibility, commercial impracticability, and pandemics/travel restrictions with prompt refunds.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: Such circumstances include government-imposed travel restrictions and advisories, epidemics and pandemics, and conditions making it unsafe or imprudent for attendees to travel or gather.

findings.finding_text: The cutoff date is set at 35 days prior to arrival, exceeding CD's preferred maximum of 21-30 days, giving the hotel a longer window before group-rate reservations are no longer guaranteed and increasing risk that attendees booking late lose access to group rate/inventory.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff date should be no earlier than 21-30 days prior to arrival.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to the group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, the Hotel will continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis.
findings.quoted_text: All reservations for rooms within the group block must be made on or before thirty-five (35) days prior to arrival.

findings.finding_text: Relocation clause matches CD's standard well, including comparable/better hotel, transportation, upgrade/welcome amenity, and pickup/commission credit. Compliant.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should receive comparable accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, upgrade/amenity on return, and full pickup/commission credit.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard. Consider adding message-forwarding language for completeness.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall relocate the affected guest to a comparable or better hotel at the Hotel's expense.

findings.finding_text: Mandatory fee disclosure clause matches CD's standard: full pre-signature disclosure required, undisclosed charges deemed waived. Compliant.
findings.cd_standard: All mandatory fees must be disclosed pre-signature; undisclosed charges are waived.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: Any mandatory charge not included in the pre-signature disclosure shall be deemed waived and the Hotel shall not bill Group for that charge.

findings.finding_text: Complimentary room ratio of 1:40 matches CD's standard and explicitly is not forfeited due to attrition. Compliant.
findings.cd_standard: One complimentary room for every 40 occupied room nights, not forfeited due to attrition.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide complimentary rooms to Group at a ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) paid room nights booked and occupied.

findings.finding_text: Assignment clause allows assignment to a successor/affiliated entity but adds a restriction not in CD's standard — the assignee must be 'in the same industry as Group' — and imposes joint-and-several liability plus Group's continuing liability for assignee default, which is more burdensome than CD's preferred fallback (assignee simply assumes obligations, event unchanged).
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign to a successor/affiliated entity without unreasonable withholding of consent, provided event terms are unchanged.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: Group may assign this agreement to a successor or affiliated management entity provided that the assignee is in the same industry as Group, is capable of performing all obligations under the agreement, and assumes all of Group's liabilities and duties in writing.

findings.finding_text: Construction/renovation clause matches CD's standard closely: no-current-plans representation, 30-day notice, termination right if interference. Missing only an arbitration mechanism for disagreement on interference, which CD standard includes.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability if renovation interferes, with arbitration available if parties disagree.
findings.proposed_language: If the parties disagree whether the work will interfere with Group's meeting, the dispute will be resolved by binding arbitration before the event dates.
findings.quoted_text: Should any renovation or construction project be scheduled to take place during or in the thirty (30) days preceding Group's event dates and materially interfere with Group's use and enjoyment of the Hotel, Group shall have the right to terminate this agreement without penalty, liability, or obligation to pay any cancellation fees.

findings.finding_text: Finance charge is capped at 1% per month, matching CD's standard. However, the clause does not clearly establish a dispute window before the finance charge applies (it separately allows 30 days to dispute but doesn't explicitly exempt disputed amounts from accruing finance charges during that window), and the prepayment provision for non-approved credit is open-ended ('stated percentage... as calculated by Hotel') rather than a defined percentage cap, contrary to CD's standard requiring a defined percentage.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charge capped at 1%/month or legal max; undisputed charges only; prepayment should be a defined percentage, not open-ended/hotel-discretionary.
findings.proposed_language: Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. If credit is not approved, prepayment of no more than [X]% of estimated charges will be required prior to arrival, with the balance due at departure.
findings.quoted_text: Where credit approval is not granted to Group, Group shall remit as prepayment an amount equal to the stated percentage of anticipated charges, as calculated by Hotel based on the room block, projected food and beverage revenue, and anticipated additional services.

findings.finding_text: Reporting/audit provisions substantially match CD's standard: weekly pickup reports, post-event report within 30 days, no-cost audit rights. Missing the specific commitment that any guest room occupied by a Group-registered attendee but not coded to Group will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid.
findings.cd_standard: Any miscoded room found in an audit should be credited to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid.
findings.proposed_language: Any guest room occupied by an individual on Group's registration list but not coded to Group within Hotel's system will be credited to Group's final pickup regardless of the rate paid.
findings.quoted_text: Group may audit the room block at no cost to itself, and may request supporting documentation including daily rooming records and charge details within sixty (60) days of receiving the post-event report.

findings.finding_text: Indemnification is mutual and limited to each party's own negligence/willful misconduct, matching CD's standard. Insurance requirement of $1M general liability appears proportionate. One gap: the clause does not explicitly include reasonable attorney's fees within the indemnification scope as CD's standard specifies.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual, limited to own negligence, and include each party's reasonable attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: To the extent permitted by law, each party will protect, indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party against claims, losses, or damages, including reasonable attorney's fees, arising out of the negligence or willful misconduct of the indemnifying party.
findings.quoted_text: each party's obligation to indemnify the other shall be limited to claims arising solely from that party's own negligence or willful misconduct.

findings.finding_text: No security deposit is required, and any damage charges are explicitly kept separate from attrition/F&B/room charges, and refund/accounting timing (30 days) matches CD's standard. Compliant.
findings.cd_standard: Any deposit should be refunded within 30 days absent documented damage and not commingled with attrition/F&B charges.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: Any damages paid shall be applied solely to documented damage expenses and to nothing else, and shall not be credited or offset against room charges, food and beverage minimums, or any other contractual obligation.

findings.finding_text: Termination for cause is limited to Group's material breach (Hotel-initiated termination) and does not appear to give Group a parallel termination-for-cause right (e.g., for Hotel's uncured breach) separate from the specific force majeure/renovation/labor/brand-change provisions. This is narrower than CD's standard, which treats termination for cause as available to protect Group broadly across several trigger events, though most of those triggers are separately covered elsewhere in this contract (renovation, brand change, labor, force majeure, named storm) with adequate termination rights.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should let the group walk away with no liability across several triggers, separate from the cancellation scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability, and Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments within five (5) business days, upon any of the following: force majeure; a labor dispute; a material change in Hotel's ownership, management, or brand; or renovation that interferes with Group's meeting — none of which trigger the cancellation liquidated-damages calculation.
findings.quoted_text: Cause means a material breach by Group that remains uncured for ten (10) days after written notice from the Hotel specifying the breach in detail.

findings.finding_text: Brand/ownership change clause matches CD's standard, including 30-day notice, 30-day termination election window, and treatment of bankruptcy/foreclosure as a change of ownership. Compliant, though it does not explicitly commit to a prompt refund timeframe (e.g., 5 business days) upon termination under this clause.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of notice of brand/ownership/management change, with a prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of the notice of termination under this clause.
findings.quoted_text: Upon receipt of notice of any change in brand, management, or ownership, Group shall have thirty (30) days within which to elect to terminate this agreement without cancellation penalty.

findings.finding_text: Named storm clause requires Group to give written cancellation notice within just twelve (12) hours of a NWS hurricane/tropical storm warning being issued, which is an unusually tight and operationally difficult notice window compared to typical industry practice, creating risk that Group loses its named-storm protection if it cannot act within half a day. Additionally, Portland, Oregon is not a coastal/hurricane-belt market, so a hurricane/tropical storm warning trigger may rarely if ever apply there, potentially leaving Group without meaningful storm protection despite having a clause that appears protective.
findings.cd_standard: Named storm clauses should have a workable notice period and cancellation window appropriate to the property's actual risk profile.
findings.proposed_language: Group must provide written notice of cancellation to the Hotel's Director of Sales within a commercially reasonable period (e.g., seventy-two (72) hours) of the National Weather Service's issuance of a relevant severe weather warning or advisory for the Portland area, and this clause should reference the storm/weather event types actually applicable to the Hotel's geographic location.
findings.quoted_text: Group must provide written notice of cancellation to the Hotel's Director of Sales within twelve (12) hours of the National Weather Service's issuance of a hurricane or tropical storm warning for the Portland area.

findings.finding_text: Attendee data clause matches CD's standard: no use for Hotel's own marketing, no sale/sharing with third parties, deletion on request. Compliant.
findings.cd_standard: Attendee data should not be used for hotel marketing or sold to third parties without consent.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel will not use attendee data for its own marketing purposes, and shall not employ such data in connection with promotional solicitations, advertising campaigns or any direct marketing initiative directed toward the attendees.

findings.finding_text: ADA clause warrants compliance and covers standard structural accommodations at Hotel's cost, but auxiliary aid costs are to be 'divided between Group and the Hotel' rather than clearly allocated by CD's standard formula (Group funds aids in its own function space; Hotel funds aids in guest rooms/public areas). This ambiguous 'divided' allocation could shift more cost to Group than CD's standard contemplates.
findings.cd_standard: Group funds auxiliary aids in function space it uses; Hotel funds auxiliary aids in guest rooms and common areas.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.
findings.quoted_text: The cost of any auxiliary aids or services requested by Group or its attendees, including but not limited to interpreters, transcription services, specialized audio equipment and accessible transportation, shall be divided between Group and the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: Governing law/venue is Group's home state, no punitive damages, each party bears own fees — fully matches CD's standard. Compliant.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law/venue should be Group's location; no punitive damages; each party bears own fees.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which Group maintains its principal offices, without regard to its conflicts of law principles.

findings.finding_text: Labor disputes clause matches CD's standard well: 12-month advance notice of CBA expiration, ongoing updates, cancellation right with no liability if a dispute occurs within 90 days of event and materially interferes. One gap: CD's standard allows cancellation regardless of whether Hotel can still technically perform, whereas this clause requires the dispute to 'materially interfere' with Group's event, a narrower and more hotel-favorable condition.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to cancel with no liability if labor dispute arises within 90 days of event, regardless of whether hotel can still technically perform.
findings.proposed_language: If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, picketing occurs, or a strike or lockout occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without liability, regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform.
findings.quoted_text: Group may cancel with no liability, penalty, or obligation to pay any fees or charges associated with this agreement if a labor dispute materially interferes with Group's ability to conduct its event or enjoy the services, amenities, and accommodations reserved.

findings.finding_text: Rate parity clause matches CD's standard fully: retroactive adjustment, all prior reservations, commission/pickup unaffected. Compliant.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should guarantee no lower public rate; retroactive adjustment without loss of commission or pickup credit.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: If a lower public rate is offered or identified during the event dates, Group's rate shall be retroactively adjusted to match the lower public rate, effective as of the date the lower rate was first offered.

findings.finding_text: Gratuity and service charge are clearly separated and disclosed as required by CD's standard: gratuity fully distributed to staff, service charge is Hotel revenue and separately itemized. Compliant, though the 22% service charge rate itself is a business term worth flagging to Group for budgeting even though it isn't a CD standards violation.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined and disclosed.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard on definitional clarity.
findings.quoted_text: Service charge is the Hotel's own revenue and shall not be considered or characterized as a gratuity or tip to staff.

findings.finding_text: Resale/mitigation duty clause matches CD's standard: active resale effort, credit against damages, records available on request, dispute rights. Compliant.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should have affirmative duty to resell canceled inventory and credit proceeds, with records available to verify.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: Upon receipt of any notice of room release or cancellation, the Hotel must actively try to resell released rooms and function space at rates equal to or greater than the Group rate.

findings.finding_text: Outside vendor clause allows Group's own vendors with no restriction and a $0.00 surcharge, matching CD's standard of no additional fee. Compliant.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use outside vendors at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: No change recommended; clause aligns with CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall pay the Hotel an outside vendor surcharge of $0.00 for each such vendor engaged.

analysis.document_notes: The contract contains a significant internal inconsistency between Section 1 (F&B minimum of $48,000) and Section 9 (F&B minimum of $40,000, with detailed shortfall/pricing terms) — these two sections appear to reference the same event but state different dollar minimums, and only Section 9 contains operative shortfall mechanics. This should be flagged to the property for clarification/correction regardless of the substantive shortfall-penalty issue noted below. Similarly, the cancellation clause's narrative text (Section 4, paragraph 1) describes a three-tier structure (0%/50%/100%) that conflicts with the five-tier table immediately following it (18%/35%/52%/63%/70%) — the table appears to be the operative schedule but the narrative was not reconciled with it. Otherwise, the document is well-organized and complete, with no illegible or missing pages apparent."

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively across the block, and the trigger threshold is 90% pickup per night rather than the 70% cumulative threshold CD negotiates for. This significantly increases Group's exposure since any single soft night creates liability even if the overall block is well-utilized. Damages are also charged at 90% of the nightly rate rather than a lower/negotiated percentage. Some favorable provisions are present (95% occupancy credit, audit rights), but the core measurement methodology is unfavorable.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should be measured cumulatively across the entire room block, triggered only below 70% pickup, with formula-based damages and audit rights.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis, and the Group's block commitment is deemed satisfied only to the extent that occupied rooms meet or exceed ninety percent (90%) of the rooms reserved for each night of the Event.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate (plus applicable tax). For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night, as already provided in this Agreement.
findings.exposure_basis: 95 rooms/night x $168 x 90% charge rate for a single soft night at 0% pickup as illustrative worst-case per-night exposure (95 x 168 x 0.90 = $14,364; if only assessed on shortfall between 70% and 90% thresholds under night-by-night methodology, e.g., a night at 75% pickup would still trigger liability under the 90% standard but not under CD's 70% cumulative standard). Figure shown reflects potential per-night liability at full vacancy under the contract's 90% threshold and rate (95 rooms x $168 x 0.90/room shortfall estimate for illustrative comparison only).

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated against gross room revenue rather than room profit (70% of rate), and the sliding scale percentages (18%-70%) apply to that full gross revenue figure, substantially increasing Group's liability. Additionally, the Hotel has no duty to mitigate/resell and credit proceeds — in fact the contract explicitly states resale revenue is retained by Hotel with no credit to Group, and rebooking with Hotel does not offset damages. This is a significant deviation from CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be based on room profit (70% of group rate), on a sliding scale, with hotel required to mitigate via resale and credit proceeds, and credit for any rebooking within a reasonable window.
findings.quoted_text: the Group shall owe liquidated damages calculated as a percentage of gross room revenue that would have been earned on the cancelled or reduced rooms, based on the nightly group rates in effect at the time of cancellation
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit — defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate — using the sliding scale set forth in this Agreement. Hotel will undertake reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those resale revenues, less substantiated transaction costs, against the cancellation fee owed by Group. Should Group rebook the Hotel for another meeting within one (1) year of the cancellation, Hotel will credit 100% of the room revenue generated by that rebooking toward the damages owed, up to the amount of damages paid.
findings.exposure_basis: Full block cancellation at 30 days or fewer prior to arrival (70% of gross revenue): 95 rooms x 3 nights x $168 x 70% = $33,516 under gross revenue basis vs. approximately $23,461 under a 70%-of-room-profit basis (95 x 3 x 168 x 0.70 x 0.70) -- gross revenue exposure figure shown is 95 rooms x 3 nights x $168 x 70% = $33,516; the higher number reflects gross vs. profit-basis calculation delta.

findings.finding_text: The contract explicitly states resale revenue from cancelled rooms is retained by the Hotel with no credit to Group, and rebooking does not reduce damages owed — directly contrary to CD's mitigation/rebooking-credit standard.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should mitigate damages by reselling canceled rooms and crediting proceeds, and credit Group for any rebooking within a reasonable window.
findings.quoted_text: Any revenue the Hotel generates by reselling rooms within the cancelled portion of the Group's block shall be retained by the Hotel with no credit applied against the Group's liquidated damages obligation. If the Group subsequently rebooks rooms with the Hotel for a different date or event, such rebooking shall not reduce or eliminate any damages already owed by the Group for the cancelled Event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those resale revenues, less substantiated transaction costs, against the cancellation fee. Should Group rebook the Hotel for another meeting within one (1) year of the cancellation, Hotel will credit 100% of the room revenue generated by that rebooking toward the damages owed, up to the amount of damages paid.

findings.finding_text: No affirmative, documented mitigation duty exists; in fact the cancellation clause affirmatively disclaims any resale credit, compounding exposure under this related clause type.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to resell canceled rooms/functions and credit proceeds against damages owed, with records available to Group.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues, less reasonable, substantiated transaction costs, against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group. Call reports, sales logs, and actual occupancy records documenting this mitigation effort will be made available to Group upon request.

findings.finding_text: The F&B minimum clause largely matches CD's standard (35% shortfall charge, 12-month pricing lock), though there is an internal inconsistency: Section 1 states the F&B minimum is $26,000, while Section 7 states it is $8,500. This discrepancy should be clarified and corrected before signature.
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimum shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap, with pricing locked no earlier than 12 months before the event.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall incur a minimum food and beverage expenditure of $8,500.00 (eight thousand five hundred dollars) during the October 19-21, 2027 event.
findings.proposed_language: Clarify and reconcile the food and beverage minimum stated in Section 1 ($26,000.00) with the amount stated in Section 7 ($8,500.00) so that a single, consistent minimum governs the Agreement.
findings.exposure_basis: Discrepancy between Section 1 stated minimum ($26,000) and Section 7 stated minimum ($8,500) creates $17,500 of ambiguity in Group's potential exposure.

findings.finding_text: This clause matches CD's standard — Group may use outside vendors with no surcharge imposed by Hotel.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use outside vendors at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall impose no surcharge, fee, or additional charge of $0.00 upon Group for the engagement of outside vendors in any of these categories.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.finding_text: Cutoff date of 30 days prior to arrival, with post-cutoff reservations subject to availability (not automatic rack rate), substantially matches CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21-30 days prior to arrival with continued group-rate availability post-cutoff, subject to availability.
findings.quoted_text: All room reservations for the Group must be made and confirmed through the Hotel's group reservations department on or before thirty (30) days prior to the Event arrival date.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.finding_text: The contract contains no walk/relocation clause addressing the Hotel's obligations if it cannot honor a confirmed reservation (comparable accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, upgrade/amenity on return, pickup credit, no attrition liability for relocated nights).
findings.cd_standard: If Hotel walks a guest, it should provide comparable lodging, transportation, message forwarding, upgrade/amenity, and credit toward Group's pickup with no attrition liability for the relocated night.
findings.proposed_language: If the Hotel is unable to accommodate any guest holding a confirmed reservation, the Hotel will, at its own expense: (a) provide accommodations at a comparable hotel as close as possible for each night the guest is displaced; (b) provide complimentary round-trip ground transportation between the Hotel and the alternate hotel; (c) forward the displaced guest's telephone messages and mail; and (d) upon the guest's return, provide upgraded accommodations if available and a welcome amenity from the General Manager. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages for any night a guest is relocated.

findings.finding_text: This clause matches CD's standard — all mandatory fees must be disclosed in writing before signature, and undisclosed fees are waived.
findings.cd_standard: All mandatory fees must be disclosed in writing before signature; undisclosed charges are waived.
findings.quoted_text: Any mandatory fee or surcharge not disclosed in writing before signature is waived and shall not be charged to Group.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.finding_text: Complimentary room formula (1 per 40 occupied rooms) matches CD's standard, including non-forfeiture provisions.
findings.cd_standard: One complimentary room for every 40 occupied room nights, cumulative, not forfeited due to shortfall.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) rooms the Hotel occupies during the event dates of October 19-21, 2027.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.finding_text: No assignment/subcontracting clause addressing Group's ability to assign the agreement to a successor management company or affiliated entity.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign the contract to a successor management company or affiliated entity without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations under this Agreement and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.

findings.finding_text: No construction/renovation disclosure or termination-for-interference clause is present in the Agreement.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should represent no current renovation plans and commit to 30 days' notice with termination right if renovation interferes with the event.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan. If Group determines the work will interfere with its meeting, Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's notice.

findings.finding_text: Master account billing terms largely match CD's standard: 30-day dispute window and 1% monthly finance charge cap, though the finance charge compounds monthly, which is slightly more onerous than a flat 1% simple charge, and the prepayment provision does not specify a defined percentage cap.
findings.cd_standard: Master account payable on invoice, 1%/month cap on undisputed late balances, defined prepayment percentage if credit not approved.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall assess a monthly finance charge of one percent (1%) on the unpaid balance, compounding monthly until paid in full
findings.proposed_language: Any finance charge on unpaid, undisputed balances will not exceed one percent (1.0%) per month on a simple (non-compounding) basis, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less. If credit is not approved, prepayment will be limited to a stated percentage of estimated charges, as specified in the Hotel's proposal, with the balance due at departure.

findings.finding_text: No weekly pickup report or post-event report requirement (rooms actualized, pace report, F&B recap) is included, though a limited attrition-specific audit right does exist under Section 2.
findings.cd_standard: Group should receive weekly pickup reports pre-cutoff and a full post-event report within 30 days, plus a no-cost room-block audit right.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting a reasonable number of days prior to the cutoff date, and a full post-event report — including rooms actualized, a reservation pace report, and a food and beverage revenue recap — within thirty (30) days of Group's departure. At Group's request, Hotel will conduct a face-to-face room block audit at no cost, comparing the Hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list.

findings.finding_text: Indemnification is mutual and limited to each party's own negligence/misconduct, matching CD's standard. Insurance requirement ($1,000,000 CGL) appears proportionate.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence, with proportionate insurance requirements.
findings.quoted_text: Each party's indemnification obligation is limited to claims arising solely from that party's own negligence or willful misconduct and shall not extend to claims arising from the other party's conduct.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.finding_text: Security deposit is set at $0.00 and is properly restricted to documented damage, not commingled with attrition/F&B shortfalls, and refundable within 30 days — matches CD's standard, and in practice creates no exposure since the deposit amount is zero.
findings.cd_standard: Deposit should be reasonable, refundable within 30 days absent documented damage, and not applied to unrelated charges.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall provide to Hotel a security deposit in the amount of zero dollars, which deposit shall be held by Hotel to secure Group's performance under this Agreement.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.finding_text: A termination-for-cause clause exists (material breach, cure period, prompt refund, no damages claim by breaching party) and operates separately from cancellation damages, which is favorable. However, the broader CD standard also contemplates termination rights tied to labor disputes, brand/ownership change, and renovation — those are handled (or not) in separate clauses/missing clauses noted elsewhere, so termination rights are incomplete as a unified protection.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause (force majeure, labor dispute, ownership/brand change, renovation) should allow Group to walk away with no liability, separate from cancellation scale.
findings.quoted_text: Termination for cause operates as a separate contractual remedy and does not invoke the cancellation damages scale set forth elsewhere in this agreement.
findings.proposed_language: Expand termination rights to explicitly include: (a) force majeure; (b) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees arising within 90 days of the Event; (c) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or bankruptcy/foreclosure; and (d) renovation that Group determines will interfere with its meeting — each entitling Group to terminate without liability and receive a prompt refund, separate from the cancellation damages scale.

findings.finding_text: No clause addresses Hotel notifying Group of a change in ownership, management, or brand affiliation, or bankruptcy/foreclosure, nor a related termination right for Group.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should notify Group within 30 days of any brand/ownership/management change or bankruptcy/foreclosure, and Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of that notice.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management company, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will inform Group in writing within thirty (30) days of such change or filing. Group may terminate this Agreement without liability within thirty (30) days of receiving that notice, with all deposits and prepayments refunded within five (5) business days.

findings.finding_text: No separate named-storm clause exists. San Antonio is inland but within the broader Texas hurricane-affected region; a general force majeure clause is present but no narrower named-storm provision with its own notice period is included.
findings.cd_standard: A separate named-storm clause with its own notice period and cancellation window should be evaluated independent of general force majeure.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm (hurricane, tropical storm) is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice, regardless of whether the storm ultimately causes physical damage to the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: No provision restricts the Hotel's use of rooming list/attendee data to reservation fulfillment purposes only, or prohibits marketing use or third-party disclosure.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list/attendee data should be used solely for reservation purposes, not for Hotel marketing or third-party disclosure without consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely for the purpose of fulfilling reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.

findings.finding_text: No ADA compliance warranty or allocation of responsibility for auxiliary aids between Hotel and Group is included in the Agreement.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should warrant ADA compliance for guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation, with mutual indemnification limited to each party's own obligations and clear division of auxiliary-aid funding responsibility.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel warrants that its guest rooms, common areas, function space, and transportation services comply with the public accommodation requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). Hotel and Group will each indemnify and hold harmless the other from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA. Group is responsible for auxiliary aids needed in its function space; Hotel is responsible for auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas.

findings.finding_text: Governing law and venue are tied to Group's location, punitive damages are excluded, and each party bears its own attorney's fees — fully matches CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law/venue should be Group's location, no punitive damages, each party bears own fees.
findings.quoted_text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which Group maintains its principal offices, and the parties irrevocably submit to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in the county or judicial district where Group is located.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.finding_text: No labor disputes clause is present addressing collective bargaining agreement expiration notice or Group's right to cancel without liability if a labor dispute arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should give advance notice of CBA expirations and prompt notice of labor disputes; Group should be able to cancel with no liability if a strike/lockout/expired CBA arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year, and will notify Group within ten (10) working days of becoming aware of any labor dispute involving Hotel's employees. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, a strike, lockout, or expired labor contract affects Hotel's union employees, Group may cancel this Agreement without liability and receive a prompt refund of all deposits.

findings.finding_text: No rate parity/guarantee provision exists ensuring the Hotel won't sell rooms to the general public at a lower rate than Group's contracted rate during event dates.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should guarantee no lower public rate during event dates, with retroactive rate matching for Group's block if violated.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted group rate during the Event dates, with the exception of qualified rates (e.g., government, airline crew). If Hotel offers a lower rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match, and such rooms will remain fully commissionable and creditable toward Group's pickup and attrition calculation.

findings.finding_text: The Agreement references food and beverage charges but does not separately define or disclose gratuity versus service charge, or specify distribution to staff.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined, with gratuity fully distributed to staff and service charge disclosed as hotel revenue.
findings.proposed_language: Any gratuity charged to Group's account will be fully distributed to the servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event. Any service charge is separate from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel to cover discretionary costs of the Event. Both charges and their respective percentages will be disclosed to Group in writing prior to the Event.

analysis.document_notes: The contract contains an internal inconsistency between Section 1 (F&B minimum stated as $26,000.00) and Section 7 (F&B minimum stated as $8,500.00) that should be reconciled with the property before signature. Otherwise the document is a complete, legible, single-property group sales agreement with numbered sections and a cancellation liquidated-damages table.

findings.quoted_text: If Group fails to occupy at least seventy-five percent (75%) of the room block reserved for the Event, Hotel shall assess attrition damages against Group in accordance with the provisions of this clause.
findings.finding_text: Attrition threshold is set at 75% pickup rather than the 70% CD standard, meaning Group becomes liable for damages sooner (a smaller shortfall triggers liability). The damages rate itself (75% of ADR) is also slightly above CD's 70% benchmark. The cumulative measurement, 95%-occupancy-night credit, and audit rights all match CD's position and are well-drafted.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should trigger only below 70% cumulative pickup, with damages at 70% of the group rate for the shortfall.
findings.proposed_language: If Group fails to occupy at least seventy percent (70%) of the room block reserved for the Event, calculated cumulatively, Hotel shall assess attrition damages equal to seventy percent (70%) of the average daily room rate multiplied by the number of unoccupied room nights representing the shortfall below that threshold.
findings.exposure_basis: Difference between 75% and 70% threshold represents an additional 5% of the 210-room peak-night block (~10-11 rooms across the event) exposed to attrition liability at $419/night that would not exist under CD's 70% standard; exact multi-night total not calculable from data given.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall provide the Hotel with a final rooming list containing all guest names, room type preferences, and arrival and departure dates no later than thirty-two (32) days prior to the Event's opening day.
findings.finding_text: Cutoff is 32 days prior to arrival, slightly outside CD's 21-30 day standard window, though the post-cutoff rate protection language is favorable. More concerning is the qualifying language stating Hotel makes 'no representation' rates will remain available and that pricing/room type post-cutoff is 'determined solely by Hotel's yield management practices,' which undercuts the commitment to honor the group rate.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be 21-30 days prior to arrival, with group rate held after cutoff subject to availability.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis, without discretion to reprice based on yield management.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall remain liable for all cancellation damages unless the cancellation occurs more than twelve (12) months prior to the Event's opening day, in which case Group shall have no liability and the block shall be released with no further obligation.
findings.finding_text: Sliding scale, resale mitigation credit, and rebooking credit all align with CD standards and the 12-month no-liability window matches CD's fallback. This clause is largely favorable; no material finding beyond noting alignment.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be a sliding scale based on lost room profit, with resale mitigation and rebooking credit, and no liability beyond 12 months prior to arrival.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause as drafted substantially matches CD's standard position.
