findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide Group with a menu and pricing proposal at least fourteen (14) months prior to the Event date, and all menu selections and per-person pricing shall be locked and shall not be subject to increase or modification after that date.
findings.finding_text: Menu pricing is locked 14 months prior to the event, exceeding CD's standard of no earlier than 12 months (favorable to hotel, not group — locking pricing earlier removes Group's ability to benefit from later, potentially lower, negotiated menus). Additionally, shortfall is billed at 40% rather than CD's 35%, and the Hotel unilaterally reserves 'the right to negotiate or waive the shortfall in its sole discretion,' which is one-sided and creates uncertainty for Group.
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimum should not be locked earlier than 12 months prior to event, with shortfall billed at 35% of the gap.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will not be established earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the $165,000.00 minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not forty percent, and the shortfall calculation shall not be subject to Hotel's unilateral discretion to negotiate or waive.
findings.exposure_basis: 5 percentage-point difference (40% vs 35%) applied to a full $165,000 shortfall scenario ($165,000 x 5% = $8,250 in additional exposure if F&B revenue were zero; actual exposure scales with shortfall size).

findings.quoted_text: Any charge, fee, or surcharge not included in the written disclosure provided prior to signature shall be automatically waived and shall not be assessed against Group, and Group shall have no obligation to pay any such undisclosed charge.
findings.finding_text: This clause fully matches CD's standard, including outright waiver of undisclosed charges and an express no-resort-fee commitment. No finding of concern.
findings.cd_standard: All mandatory fees must be disclosed pre-signature; undisclosed charges are waived.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: The complimentary room ratio is forty-five (45), meaning that for every forty-five (45) paid room nights generated by Group, the Hotel shall provide one (1) complimentary room night at no charge to Group.
findings.finding_text: Ratio of 1:45 is less favorable than CD's standard 1:40, meaning Group must generate more room nights to earn the same complimentary room credit. All other aspects (automatic accrual, no forfeiture on shortfall) are favorable and match CD's position.
findings.cd_standard: One complimentary room for every 40 occupied, revenue-producing room nights, calculated cumulatively.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block.
findings.exposure_basis: Exposure depends on final pickup; at full 210-room peak block occupied across 4 nights (~840 total room nights, though full block size across all nights not specified), the 1:45 vs 1:40 ratio difference would reduce comp rooms earned by roughly 10-15%, but total room nights across all event dates are not specified precisely enough to calculate a dollar figure.

findings.quoted_text: The Monarch shall assess a monthly finance charge of 1.3% on any portion of an undisputed invoice balance remaining unpaid thirty (30) days after the invoice due date.
findings.finding_text: Finance charge of 1.3% per month exceeds CD's cap of 1.0% per month or legal maximum, whichever is less. Additionally, the dispute window is only 12 days (versus CD's 30-day standard), and prepayment absent credit approval is set at 75% of estimated charges rather than a more limited defined percentage.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charge capped at 1% per month or legal max, whichever is less; 30-day dispute window before finance charges accrue; defined, moderate prepayment percentage if credit not approved.
findings.proposed_language: A finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to unpaid, undisputed balances thirty (30) days after invoice. Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues. If credit is not approved, prepayment will not exceed 50% of estimated charges.

findings.quoted_text: The service charge is not a gratuity, tip, or compensation to service staff, and Group acknowledges that the Hotel retains the entire service charge amount for its own account.
findings.finding_text: Clause clearly distinguishes gratuity (fully distributed to staff) from service charge (hotel revenue) and discloses both percentages, matching CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity fully distributed to staff; service charge disclosed as separate hotel revenue.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the Group's right to engage outside vendors, the Group shall remit to the Hotel an outside vendor surcharge in the amount of "$0.00". This surcharge shall be payable in full upon execution of this Agreement and represents the Hotel's sole additional compensation for the privilege of hosting outside vendors on the Hotel's premises during the Event.
findings.finding_text: Although the surcharge amount is stated as $0.00, the clause as drafted structurally imposes a mandatory 'outside vendor surcharge' as a matter of contract right, meaning the Hotel could argue this fee framework permits it to fill in or later invoice a nonzero surcharge, or that the concept of a vendor surcharge is contractually validated. Even at $0.00 currently, this creates a template for a fee that CD's standard says should not exist at all — the right to use outside vendors should be at no additional fee or surcharge, full stop, not merely a surcharge set to zero in this instance.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use outside vendors at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for audio-visual, decorating, security, and transportation services. Hotel shall not impose any outside vendor surcharge, and this Agreement shall not include any fee mechanism, even if currently set at zero, that could later be invoked to charge such a fee.
findings.exposure_basis: Surcharge is currently stated as $0.00, so no immediate dollar exposure, but the clause structure creates risk of a fee being applied in future dealings or amendments.

findings.quoted_text: The indemnification obligation of each party shall be limited to claims arising solely from that party's own negligence or willful misconduct.
findings.finding_text: Indemnification is mutual and limited to each party's own negligence, matching CD's standard. Insurance requirement of $2,500,000 per occurrence appears proportionate for an event of this size (210-room peak block, four-night conference).
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence; insurance proportionate to event size.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: the cost of such auxiliary aids shall be divided between the Group and the Hotel... the parties shall negotiate in good faith to determine the appropriate allocation of costs for each specific auxiliary aid
findings.finding_text: CD's standard calls for a clear division of funding responsibility (Group funds aids in its function space; Hotel funds aids in guest rooms/common areas), but this contract instead requires ad hoc negotiation over cost allocation for every auxiliary aid, creating uncertainty and potential unbudgeted cost exposure for Group.
findings.cd_standard: Clear division: Group funds auxiliary aids in function space it controls; Hotel funds aids in guest rooms and common areas.
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Both parties will communicate known auxiliary-aid needs to the other in advance of the Event.

findings.quoted_text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which Group maintains its principal offices, without regard to its conflict of law principles.
findings.finding_text: Governing law, venue, no-punitive-damages, and each-party-bears-own-fees provisions all match CD's standard favoring Group's home jurisdiction.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law/venue should be Group's location, no punitive damages, each party bears own fees.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide written notice to the Group of any expiration, non-renewal, or material breach in any collective bargaining agreement, union contract, or labor agreement covering employees at the Hotel no later than nine (9) months prior to the expiration date of such agreement.
findings.finding_text: Advance notice of CBA expiration is 9 months rather than CD's standard of a full year, giving Group slightly less lead time to plan around potential labor disruption. The cancellation right itself (75-day window, no liability) is actually broader/more generous than CD's 90-day-prior-to-event trigger standard, so this is a minor, mixed finding.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should give a year's advance notice of CBA expiration dates; cancellation right if labor dispute arises within 90 days of event.
findings.proposed_language: The Hotel shall provide written notice to Group of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates one (1) year in advance.

findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall undertake active and good faith efforts to resell such released accommodations and facilities at prevailing market rates
findings.finding_text: Resale mitigation duty is affirmative, documented, and verifiable, matching CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should have an affirmative, documented duty to resell canceled inventory and credit proceeds, with records available to Group.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: Any security deposit or other funds held by the Hotel shall be applied solely to the repair or replacement of documented damage to Hotel property and to nothing else, and shall not be applied to room charges, food and beverage charges, incidental fees, or any other obligation of Group under this Agreement.
findings.finding_text: No deposit is charged, and any future deposit is properly ring-fenced from other charges with a defined dispute and refund process, matching CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Damage deposit should be reasonable, refundable within a defined window, and not commingled with other charges.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: Any night spent at the alternative accommodation shall be credited to Group's room pickup and shall count toward all occupancy and pickup thresholds stated in this Agreement, and shall be credited to all commissions or rebates calculated on the basis of room pickup, occupancy, or other similar metrics.
findings.finding_text: Comparable/better accommodations, transportation, upgrade/amenity on return, and pickup/commission credit are all present, matching CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Walked guests should receive comparable accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, upgrade/amenity, and pickup credit with no attrition liability for Group.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: If any renovation, construction, or capital project undertaken by the Hotel will materially interfere with the Group's ability to conduct its Event as contemplated by this Agreement, the Group may terminate this Agreement without penalty, liability, or further obligation
findings.finding_text: Representation of no current plans, 30-day notice, and termination right without liability all match CD's standard. No arbitration mechanism for disputed interference is included, a minor gap relative to CD's fallback language.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should represent no current renovation plans and provide 30 days notice with termination right if interference; arbitration available for disputes.
findings.proposed_language: If the parties disagree whether the work will interfere with Group's event, the dispute will be resolved by binding arbitration prior to the event dates.

findings.quoted_text: Termination for cause pursuant to this clause shall operate independently of and shall not trigger the cancellation damages, liquidated damages, or other remedies set forth in the cancellation clause of this Agreement.
findings.finding_text: This section as drafted addresses Hotel's termination for Group's breach, which is standard and not the focus of CD's concern (Group's right to terminate for cause). Group's termination-for-cause rights are instead separately addressed in Force Majeure (6), Named Storm (7), Construction (17), Change of Brand (18), and Labor Relations (19) sections, each of which independently grants no-liability termination and prompt refund, satisfying CD's standard in substance even though scattered across multiple clauses rather than consolidated.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause (force majeure, labor dispute, ownership change, renovation) should allow Group to walk away with no liability and prompt refund, separate from cancellation damages.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed in substance; consider consolidating Group's termination-for-cause rights into a single section for clarity.

findings.location_section: 18. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership
findings.quoted_text: The Group's termination right shall be conditioned upon the Group demonstrating, in good faith, that the change materially affects the Hotel's ability to perform its obligations under this Agreement or materially alters the character or service standards of the property.
findings.finding_text: CD's standard grants termination 'at Group's sole discretion' upon notice of a brand/ownership/management change, but this contract conditions the termination right on Group affirmatively demonstrating material effect on performance or service standards — a materiality burden not present in CD's fallback language, which could be used by the Hotel to contest Group's exercise of the right.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of notice of change in ownership/management/brand, at its sole discretion.
findings.proposed_language: Upon receipt of notice of a change in brand, management, or ownership, Group may, at its sole discretion, terminate this Agreement without penalty or liability within thirty (30) days of such notice, with no requirement to demonstrate material impact.

findings.quoted_text: The commission payable to Group's travel agent or booking agent, and any pickup credit or other room revenue rebate accrued by Group under separate provisions of this Agreement, shall be calculated on the basis of Group's room revenue as originally stated and shall not be recalculated, reduced, or adjusted downward as a result of any retroactive rate adjustment made pursuant to the rate parity clause.
findings.finding_text: Rate parity clause is strong and fully matches CD's standard, including retroactive rate matching and preservation of commission/pickup credit.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should guarantee no lower public rate, adjust retroactively, without losing commission or pickup credit.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: Conditions that render it unsafe or imprudent for the Group's attendees to travel to New York or to gather in person at the Hotel, whether arising from public health directives, governmental restrictions, or other circumstances beyond the parties' reasonable control, shall constitute a force majeure event relieving the affected party's performance obligations.
findings.finding_text: Force majeure clause comprehensively covers government travel restrictions/advisories, epidemics/pandemics, and unsafe-to-travel conditions, with prompt deposit refund, matching CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should cover illegality/impossibility/impracticability including travel restrictions, pandemics, and unsafe conditions, with prompt refund.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: A named storm cancellation window of sixty (60) hours prior to the first event date shall apply, during which either party may cancel this Agreement without penalty if the named storm warning or advisory remains in effect for the scheduled dates
findings.finding_text: Named storm clause is present as a distinct provision with its own window (60 hours) and cancellation mechanics, consistent with CD's standard that this be treated separately from general force majeure.
findings.cd_standard: Named storm clause should exist separately from general force majeure with its own notice/cancellation window.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not use any attendee data, including names, contact information, demographic information, and attendance records, for the Hotel's own marketing purposes or for any promotional activity conducted by the Hotel or its affiliates.
findings.finding_text: Clause fully matches CD's standard prohibiting hotel marketing use or third-party disclosure of attendee data.
findings.cd_standard: Attendee data should not be used by hotel for marketing or sold to third parties without consent.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

findings.quoted_text: Group shall have the right, at its own expense and upon reasonable notice to the Hotel, to engage an independent auditor to audit the room block records, billing records, and attendance records maintained by the Hotel in connection with this Agreement, and Group may conduct such audit at no cost to the Hotel beyond providing reasonable access to such records.
findings.finding_text: Weekly pickup reports (starting 8 weeks prior), post-event report within 30 days, and audit rights are all present, matching CD's standard substantially. Note the audit is at Group's own expense, whereas CD's standard calls for a no-cost audit right, a minor deviation.
findings.cd_standard: Group should receive weekly pickup reports, full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost room-block audit right.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request, Hotel will conduct a face-to-face room block audit at no cost, comparing the Hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list.

findings.quoted_text: Group may assign this Agreement to any successor entity or affiliated management organization that assumes all of Group's obligations hereunder without the Hotel's prior consent
findings.finding_text: Assignment clause matches CD's standard, permitting assignment to successor/affiliated management entities without consent.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign to successor management company or affiliated entity without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.

analysis.document_notes: The contract is well-organized and unusually thorough relative to industry norms, with most clauses closely tracking CD's standard fallback language (e.g., resale mitigation, rate parity, force majeure, named storm, attendee data, damage deposit, walk/relocation). The primary areas of financial exposure are: (1) the attrition threshold set at 75% rather than CD's 70% benchmark; (2) F&B shortfall billed at 40% instead of 35%, compounded by unilateral hotel discretion to waive/negotiate the shortfall; (3) a 1.3% monthly finance charge exceeding CD's 1.0% cap, paired with a short 12-day invoice dispute window and a high 75% prepayment requirement absent credit approval; (4) a complimentary room ratio of 1:45 versus CD's 1:40; and (5) an outside-vendor surcharge clause that, while currently set at $0.00, retains a contractual fee mechanism CD's standard says should not exist at all. No pages were illegible; Schedule A referenced in the cancellation clause was reproduced as a table and reviewed in full."

findings.finding_text: Menu pricing is locked for 24 months (exceeding CD's 12-month standard, exposing Group to stale pricing risk both ways), and any F&B shortfall is billed at 100% (Group guarantees 80% of projected revenue and must pay full shortfall dollar-for-dollar), rather than a fraction such as 35%.
findings.cd_standard: F&B minimums should lock pricing no earlier than 12 months out, and shortfalls should be billed at a fraction (35%) of the gap, not dollar-for-dollar.
findings.proposed_language: Menu prices for the Event's food and beverage functions will not be established earlier than twelve (12) months prior to the Event. If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the guaranteed minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall.
findings.quoted_text: If the Group's actual food and beverage charges, when totaled for the entire Event Period, fall short of the guaranteed minimum amount, the Group shall pay to the Hotel the shortfall within thirty (30) days of final invoice.
findings.exposure_basis: Full $96,000 F&B minimum could be billed dollar-for-dollar as shortfall rather than at 35% per CD standard, an exposure difference of up to $62,400.

findings.finding_text: Group is required to use only Hotel's in-house or approved vendors, or pay a $2,500 per-vendor/category surcharge for outside vendors, contrary to CD's position that Group should be free to use outside vendors at no additional fee.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use outside vendors of choice at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, exhibit decorating, security, floral, transportation, and tours. Hotel's in-house vendors are not mandatory for any service category.
findings.quoted_text: Group's use of outside vendors not approved in advance by the Hotel shall be subject to a surcharge of $2,500.00 per outside vendor service or vendor category, which surcharge shall be assessed in addition to any other charges imposed under this Agreement
findings.exposure_basis: Surcharge per unapproved outside vendor category; exposure scales with number of vendor categories used.

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night (not cumulatively), the liability threshold is 80% (vs. CD's 70%), full-block-sellout credit only applies at 100% occupancy (vs. CD's 95%), and Group has no audit or dispute rights over the Hotel's occupancy determinations, which are stated to be 'final and binding.'
findings.cd_standard: Attrition should be measured cumulatively with an 70% pickup threshold, 95%-occupancy nights get full credit, and Group should have audit rights and formula-based (not discretionary) damages.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment. At Group's request, Hotel will provide supporting occupancy records to verify the calculation, and Group shall retain the right to audit and dispute the Hotel's occupancy determinations.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's calculation of attrition damages shall be final and binding on Group, and Group shall have no right to inspect, audit, or challenge the Hotel's occupancy records or the Hotel's determination of room nights sold, occupied, or available on any night during the Event.
findings.exposure_basis: 275 rooms x $189/night x 80% liability rate = maximum exposure per unoccupied night at full block shortfall (275 x $189 x 0.80)

findings.finding_text: Cancellation damages are calculated on gross room revenue (not 70% room profit as CD standard requires), the Hotel is not obligated to mitigate/resell and expressly retains all resale proceeds without credit to Group, no credit is given for rebooking, and there is no liability-free cancellation window even far in advance (365+ days still carries 20% liability) — all contrary to CD standard.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be sliding scale on room profit (70% of rate), hotel must mitigate via resale and credit proceeds, rebooking credit should apply, and no liability more than 12 months out.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit—defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate—on a sliding scale, with no liability for cancellation more than twelve (12) months prior to arrival. Hotel will undertake reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and will credit resale revenues, less substantiated costs, against the cancellation fee. Should Group rebook the Hotel within one (1) year of cancellation, Hotel will credit 100% of the rebooking's room revenue toward damages owed.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall retain any revenue earned by reselling cancelled rooms to other guests, and such resale revenue shall not be credited against Group's liquidated damages obligation in any manner or to any extent.
findings.exposure_basis: Max exposure at 80% of gross room revenue for full block: 275 rooms x 4 nights x $189 x 80% = $148,005 (illustrative worst case for late cancellation)

findings.finding_text: Force majeure explicitly excludes government-imposed travel restrictions and advisories from excusing performance, contrary to CD standard which requires these be included. Also, deposits are retained entirely by the Hotel with no refund obligation upon force majeure invocation, contrary to CD's prompt-refund standard.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should include government travel restrictions/advisories, epidemics, and unsafe-travel conditions, with prompt refund of deposits.
findings.proposed_language: Force majeure includes government regulation, restriction, or advisory (mandatory or advisory in nature) affecting travel or assembly, epidemic or pandemic, and conditions making travel or assembly unsafe or imprudent. Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither government-imposed travel restrictions nor government travel advisories of any kind, whether mandatory or advisory in character, shall be deemed a force majeure event excusing or limiting the obligations of Group under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Cutoff date is set at 45 days prior to arrival, exceeding CD's recommended 21-30 day window, and reservations after cutoff are not available at group rate regardless of availability — they revert to rack rate outright.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21-30 days prior to arrival, with post-cutoff reservations still available at group rate subject to availability.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to the group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, the Hotel will continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis.
findings.quoted_text: All room reservations on behalf of Group must be requested and confirmed by the Hotel no later than forty-five (45) days prior to the Event check-in date of July 13, 2027.

findings.finding_text: Relocated guests bear their own transportation costs and arrangements, receive no upgrade or welcome amenity upon return, and the relocated night is expressly excluded from Group's pickup/commission credit and (implicitly) from attrition credit — all contrary to CD's standard that the Hotel should bear these costs and the night should count toward Group's block with no attrition liability.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel walking a reservation should provide comparable/better accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, upgrade/amenity on return, and count the night toward pickup with no attrition liability to Group.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel is unable to accommodate a guaranteed reservation, Hotel will, at its own expense, provide comparable or better accommodations, complimentary round-trip transportation, forward messages, and provide an upgrade and welcome amenity upon the guest's return. Each relocated room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and commission, and Group will not be liable for attrition damages for any relocated night.
findings.quoted_text: The affected guest shall bear full responsibility for all transportation costs to and from any alternative hotel arranged pursuant to a walk relocation.

findings.finding_text: Hotel reserves right to assess additional fees/surcharges at any time post-signature at its sole discretion, and expressly states Group remains liable even for charges not disclosed prior to signature — directly contrary to CD's standard that undisclosed charges should be waived.
findings.cd_standard: All mandatory fees must be disclosed in writing before signing; undisclosed charges should be waived.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will disclose in writing, prior to execution of this Agreement, all charges associated with the Event, including resort fees, surcharges, and service fees. Any charge not disclosed to Group in writing prior to signature is waived.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding any other provision, Group remains liable for all charges assessed by Hotel, whether or not such charges were disclosed in writing prior to execution of this Agreement. Hotel's failure to disclose any fee or surcharge before signature shall not relieve Group of its obligation to pay such charge upon invoice.

findings.finding_text: Complimentary room ratio is 1:80 (vs. CD's 1:40), is described as a mere 'guideline' not a commitment, is subject to Hotel's sole discretion to withhold/reduce, and is forfeited entirely (not prorated) if Group's pickup falls short.
findings.cd_standard: Complimentary rooms should be earned on a clear, cumulative 1:40 formula regardless of hotel discretion or attrition elsewhere.
findings.proposed_language: Group will receive one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) occupied, revenue-producing room nights actualized, calculated cumulatively across the entire room block, regardless of whether the contracted block was otherwise met.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall consider providing complimentary guestroom accommodations to Group at a ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every eighty (80) occupied rooms successfully billed during the Event, provided Group achieves full pickup of its contracted room block.

findings.finding_text: Assignment is barred entirely without Hotel's prior written consent, which may be withheld in Hotel's sole and absolute discretion for any reason or no reason — contrary to CD's standard permitting assignment to a successor management company without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign to a successor management/affiliated entity without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.proposed_language: Group may assign this Agreement to a successor association management company or affiliated entity without Hotel's consent, provided the assignee assumes all obligations and the event dates, room block, and program remain substantially unchanged. Any other assignment requires Hotel's consent, not to be unreasonably withheld.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's consent to any proposed assignment or transfer shall be entirely within the Hotel's sole and absolute discretion, and the Hotel may withhold consent to an assignment for any reason whatsoever or for no reason stated.

findings.finding_text: Hotel disclaims any representation about renovation plans, may commence renovation at any time including during the Event without notice, and Group waives any right to terminate or claim damages/abatement — contrary to CD's standard requiring representation of no current plans, 30-day notice, and termination right if the work interferes.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should represent no current renovation plans, give 30 days' notice with mitigation plan, and Group should be able to terminate without liability if it interferes.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation affecting facilities to be used by Group. If Hotel later confirms such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days describing scope, schedule, impact, and mitigation plan. If the work will interfere with Group's meeting, Group may terminate without liability.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall have the right to commence renovation work at the Hotel at any time, including during the Event, without providing Group advance notice of any kind, and Group shall have no right to object to or restrict such work based on timing, noise, dust, disruption, or any other impact on Group's event or its attendees.

findings.finding_text: Contract states there is 'no period in which Group may dispute a charge' and imposes a 1.5% monthly compounding finance charge (exceeding CD's 1% cap), and allows Hotel to require prepayment in 'whatever amount it determines' if credit is not approved, with no defined percentage cap.
findings.cd_standard: Master account should be payable on invoice with a real dispute window before finance charges apply; finance charge capped at 1%/month; prepayment should be a defined percentage if credit not approved.
findings.proposed_language: Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of the final itemized invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues. Any finance charge on unpaid, undisputed balances will not exceed one percent (1.0%) per month or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less. If credit is not approved, prepayment will be limited to a defined percentage (e.g. 50%) of estimated charges.
findings.quoted_text: All invoiced amounts shall be due and payable in full when due, with no period in which Group may dispute a charge.

findings.finding_text: Group has no right to audit, inspect, or independently verify Hotel's room block or pickup records; pickup reports are furnished at Hotel's 'sole discretion and convenience' rather than guaranteed; there is no weekly pickup report requirement.
findings.cd_standard: Group should receive weekly pickup reports, a full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost audit right against Hotel's occupancy records.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group a weekly guestroom pickup report starting a set number of days prior to cutoff, and a full post-event report within thirty (30) days of departure. At Group's request, Hotel will conduct a face-to-face room block audit at no cost, comparing Hotel's in-house guest list against Group's registration list.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have no right to audit, inspect, or independently verify the room block records maintained by the Hotel, nor shall Group have any right to engage a third-party auditor or representative to examine the Hotel's reservation systems, registration records, or billing documentation.

findings.finding_text: Indemnification is one-sided: Group indemnifies Hotel even for Hotel's own ordinary negligence (only excluding Hotel's gross negligence/willful misconduct), and Hotel has zero indemnification obligation to Group — contrary to CD's mutual, negligence-based indemnification standard.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual and limited to each party's own negligence/willful misconduct; Group should never indemnify Hotel for Hotel's own negligence.
findings.proposed_language: Each party will indemnify, defend, and hold harmless the other party against claims arising out of the indemnifying party's own negligence or willful misconduct. Neither party indemnifies the other for that other party's own negligence.
findings.quoted_text: Group's indemnity obligations extend to and include claims arising from the Hotel's own negligence, ordinary or gross, provided that Group shall not be obligated to indemnify the Hotel for claims arising solely from the Hotel's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

findings.finding_text: The $25,000 security deposit may be applied at Hotel's sole discretion against attrition, F&B shortfalls, cancellation fees, and other charges — directly contrary to CD's standard that deposits should not offset attrition/cancellation/F&B minimums — and refund window is 90 days rather than 30.
findings.cd_standard: Damage deposits should be reasonable, refundable within 30 days absent documented damage, and not commingled with unrelated charges like attrition or F&B minimums.
findings.proposed_language: The security deposit will be refunded in full within thirty (30) days of the event's conclusion unless Hotel provides an itemized accounting of specific documented damage. The deposit may not be applied toward attrition, cancellation, or F&B minimum shortfalls.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel shall apply the deposit, in its sole discretion, against attrition charges, food and beverage shortfalls, damage to Hotel property, unpaid room charges, cancellation fees, or any other amounts owed by Group to Hotel under this Agreement or otherwise.
findings.exposure_basis: Full security deposit amount stated in the contract, at risk of being applied to unrelated charges.

findings.finding_text: The contract provides no standalone no-liability termination right for force majeure, labor disputes, or ownership change separate from the cancellation damages scale; instead Article 8 explicitly states any Group termination — 'irrespective of the cause' — is treated as a cancellation subject to the full liquidated damages scale.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause (force majeure, labor dispute, ownership/brand change, interfering renovation) should allow Group to walk away with no liability, separate from the cancellation damages scale.
findings.proposed_language: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability upon: (a) force majeure; (b) a labor dispute involving Hotel's employees; (c) a material change in Hotel's ownership, management, or brand; or (d) renovation interfering with Group's meeting. None of the foregoing triggers the liquidated-damages calculation in the cancellation clause.
findings.quoted_text: Any termination of this Agreement by the Group, irrespective of the cause or justification asserted by the Group, shall be treated as a cancellation by the Group under the cancellation damages scale set forth in Article 8, and the Group shall pay to the Hotel the cancellation damages calculated in accordance with that scale based on the date on which the termination notice is delivered.

findings.finding_text: While a 90-day notice and 10-day termination right exist for brand/ownership/management change, the clause explicitly excludes bankruptcy, receivership, foreclosure, or insolvency-related events from triggering any notice or termination right — contrary to CD's standard which includes bankruptcy/foreclosure.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability within 30 days of notice of ownership/brand/management change, bankruptcy, or foreclosure.
findings.proposed_language: Should Hotel undergo a material change in ownership, management, or brand affiliation, or file for bankruptcy, or have foreclosure occur, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days. Group may terminate without liability within thirty (30) days of that notice, and Hotel will refund deposits within five (5) business days.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither bankruptcy, receivership, foreclosure, assignment for benefit of creditors, nor any other proceedings or event arising from the financial distress or insolvency of Hotel or its parent, affiliate, or operating company shall trigger any notice obligation or afford Group any right of termination, cancellation, or offset
findings.location_section: 18. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership

findings.finding_text: Named storm clause exists with a 24-hour warning window before arrival, narrower than CD's suggested 72-hour window, potentially leaving less time for Group to make a cancellation decision.
findings.cd_standard: Named storm clause should allow cancellation without liability if a storm is forecast to affect the hotel within 72 hours of event dates.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, either party may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice.
findings.quoted_text: If the National Weather Service issues a named storm warning for the geographic area in which the Hotel is located at any time during the period commencing twenty-four (24) hours before the start of the Event

findings.finding_text: Hotel may use Attendee Information for its own marketing purposes and share it with affiliates/marketing partners without Group's consent, contrary to CD's standard that attendee data should not be used for Hotel's own marketing or shared without Group's consent.
findings.cd_standard: Rooming list/attendee data should not be used for hotel's own marketing or shared with third parties without Group's consent.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will use rooming list and attendee data solely to fulfill reservations under this Agreement. Hotel will not use such data for its own marketing purposes, nor disclose it to any third party, without Group's prior written consent.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may use Attendee Information for its own marketing purposes, including but not limited to direct mail, email, and telephonic solicitation of the attendees who registered for the Event.

findings.finding_text: ADA warranty is present, but auxiliary-aid cost allocation is vaguely split ('baseline' vs. 'incremental/specialized') rather than the clear division CD recommends (Group funds function space aids, Hotel funds guest rooms/common areas), and undisclosed accessibility needs may be billed to Group at Hotel's 'sole discretion' without a clear indemnification provision for each party's own ADA obligations.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should warrant ADA compliance with each party indemnifying only its own ADA obligations, and clear division of auxiliary aid funding (Group funds function space, Hotel funds guest rooms/common areas).
findings.proposed_language: Group is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids needed in the function space held for its use; Hotel is responsible for obtaining and funding any auxiliary aids required by law in guest rooms, public space, and common areas. Hotel and Group will each indemnify the other only for that party's own ADA obligations.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall provide baseline auxiliary aids that are considered standard for its operations, while Group shall bear responsibility for the incremental cost of specialized or unusual accommodations tailored specifically to the Event and its participants' particular needs

findings.finding_text: Governing law/venue is the Hotel's location (Marion County, Indiana) rather than Group's location, and the Hotel is entitled to punitive/exemplary damages plus attorney's fees against Group, while Group has no reciprocal right — contrary to CD standard of Group's home state/venue, no punitive damages, and each party bearing its own fees.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law/venue should be Group's location, no punitive damages, and each party bears own attorney's fees.
findings.proposed_language: This Agreement will be construed under the laws of the state in which Group is located, with disputes venued in the city where Group is located. Any award will be limited to actual damages; punitive damages will not be awarded. Each party will bear its own attorney's fees.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall be entitled to recover punitive damages, exemplary damages, and all consequential and incidental damages available under applicable law, in addition to actual damages, in any action arising out of the Group's breach or willful misconduct.

findings.finding_text: Hotel has no obligation to disclose collective bargaining expiration dates or notify Group of labor disputes, and Group has no cancellation right at all in the event of a strike, lockout, or labor disturbance — contrary to CD's standard requiring advance notice and a no-liability cancellation right within 90 days of the event.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should give advance notice of CBA expirations and labor disputes; Group should be able to cancel with no liability if a labor dispute arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of collective bargaining agreement expiration dates annually, and will notify Group within ten (10) working days of any labor dispute. If a strike, lockout, or expired labor contract arises within ninety (90) days of the Event, Group may cancel without liability.
findings.quoted_text: In the event of any labor dispute, labor action, labor disruption, strike, work stoppage, lockout, or labor disturbance affecting the Hotel or its operations during the Event or in the days immediately preceding the Event, such occurrence shall not relieve Group of any obligation under this Agreement, shall not entitle Group to damages or credits, and shall not furnish grounds for termination or cancellation

findings.finding_text: Hotel expressly reserves the right to sell rooms at lower rates without any obligation to adjust Group's rate, disclaims 'most favored customer' protections, and any adjusted rate offered is expressly made non-commissionable and not creditable toward Group's pickup/rebate calculations — contrary to CD's standard requiring rate matching (including retroactive) without loss of commission or pickup credit.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should guarantee no lower public rate during event dates; if breached, Group's rate should be adjusted (including retroactively) without losing commission/pickup credit.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel guarantees it will not sell guestrooms at a rate lower than Group's contracted rate during the Event dates, except for qualified rates. If Hotel offers a lower rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block, and such rooms remain fully commissionable and creditable toward Group's pickup.
findings.quoted_text: Any adjusted rate made available to Group following identification of a lower public rate shall be treated as a non-commissionable rate and shall not be credited toward Group's room block pickup, occupancy targets, or performance metrics

findings.finding_text: Gratuity and service charge (24% combined) are used interchangeably with no distinction, and the Hotel may retain all or any portion as its own revenue rather than distributing to staff, with no disclosure requirement — contrary to CD's standard requiring gratuity be fully distributed to staff and service charge (hotel revenue) be clearly disclosed as separate.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity should be fully distributed to staff; service charge is separate hotel revenue and should be clearly disclosed as such.
findings.proposed_language: Any gratuity charged to Group's account will be fully distributed to servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event. Any service charge is separate from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel; both charges and their percentages will be disclosed to Group in writing prior to the Event.
findings.quoted_text: The terms 'gratuity' and 'service charge' are used interchangeably throughout this Agreement and do not constitute separately defined charges.
findings.exposure_basis: 24% of $96,000 F&B minimum = $23,040 in combined gratuity/service charge with no guaranteed staff distribution.

findings.finding_text: Hotel has expressly no obligation to attempt to resell released rooms/function space, retains all resale proceeds without credit to Group, and Group has no audit or review right over resale efforts — directly contrary to CD's standard of an affirmative, documented mitigation duty with credited proceeds and available records.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should have an affirmative duty to resell canceled rooms/functions and credit proceeds against damages owed, with records available to Group.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel will undertake all reasonable efforts to resell canceled rooms and food and beverage functions, and will credit those revenues, less substantiated transaction costs, against any cancellation or attrition damages owed by Group. Records documenting this mitigation effort will be made available to Group upon request.
findings.quoted_text: Upon release of rooms or function space by Group, the Hotel shall have no obligation to attempt to resell such released inventory, and Group waives any right to require the Hotel to undertake resale efforts or to mitigate damages

analysis.document_notes: This is a comprehensively one-sided hotel-favorable agreement (Crossroads Convention Hotel / Interstate Freight Brokers Federation, Indianapolis, July 13-16, 2027). Nearly every clause deviates substantially from CD's standard position, often with explicit disclaimers of Group's audit, dispute, mitigation-credit, and termination rights. Notably, Article 8 (Termination for Cause) cross-references 'Article 8' for the cancellation damages scale, but the cancellation damages scale actually appears in Article 4 — an apparent internal cross-reference error in the contract that should be flagged to the property for clarification. Exposure amounts calculated below are illustrative maximums based on figures stated in the contract (block size, rate, F&B minimum) and are not predictions of actual liability, which would depend on actual pickup/performance."

findings.finding_text: The shortfall formula is not tied to the F&B minimum shortfall at all — it is calculated as 35% of Group's total ROOM revenue for the event, an unrelated and potentially much larger figure than 35% of the F&B gap CD's standard contemplates. This appears to be a drafting substitution that converts a modest F&B shortfall penalty into an exposure keyed to total room revenue.
findings.cd_standard: Shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap between actual F&B revenue and the minimum, not a percentage of an unrelated revenue stream.
findings.proposed_language: If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the $155,000.00 minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual F&B revenue and the minimum, not 35% of Group's room revenue or any other unrelated figure.
findings.quoted_text: The shortfall shall be calculated as thirty-five percent (35%) of the Group's total room revenue for the Event period.
findings.exposure_basis: Cannot calculate without knowing actual room revenue generated; formula ties shortfall to total room revenue rather than the $155,000 F&B minimum gap, making exposure potentially unbounded relative to actual F&B underperformance.

findings.finding_text: Contract mandates use of Hotel's in-house/exclusive vendors for AV, telecom, floral, décor, and entertainment, and imposes a flat $3,200 per-vendor surcharge if Group wants to use an outside vendor, contrary to CD's no-fee open-vendor standard.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use outside vendors of choice at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: Group reserves the right to utilize the supplier of its choice, at no additional service fee or surcharge, for services or rentals including but not limited to audio-visual, telecommunications, floral, décor, and entertainment. Hotel's in-house vendors are not mandatory for any service category, and no per-vendor surcharge will apply.
findings.quoted_text: Any request by Group to retain an outside vendor not approved by the Hotel in writing shall be subject to a surcharge of $3,200.00 per outside vendor, which surcharge shall be payable by Group to the Hotel within ten (10) days of invoice.
findings.exposure_basis: Flat surcharge per outside vendor engaged, as stated in the contract.

findings.finding_text: Attrition clause largely matches CD standard (cumulative measurement, 70% threshold, 70% ADR damages, 95% occupancy credit, audit rights). One deviation: the audit cost-shifting provision (Group pays for audit unless discrepancies found) is not part of CD's standard, which calls for hotel to simply provide records to verify calculation without conditioning cost on outcome.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have audit rights without being charged for the audit unless it is unreasonable; CD's standard calls for hotel to provide supporting records on request.
findings.proposed_language: At Group's request, Hotel will provide supporting occupancy records to verify the attrition calculation at no cost to Group.
findings.quoted_text: Any audit shall be conducted at Group's expense if the Hotel's records are found to be accurate, and at the Hotel's expense if material discrepancies are discovered.

findings.finding_text: Cancellation clause largely tracks CD's sliding-scale, mitigation, and rebooking-credit standard, and includes a 12-month no-liability window. However, it contains a forfeiture condition not in CD's standard: Group loses rebooking credit entirely if the new event is booked at a rate 'materially lower than market rate' — a subjective, hotel-controlled standard that could void the credit CD expects Group to receive.
findings.cd_standard: Rebooking within a reasonable window should generate a 100% credit toward damages without conditions based on the hotel's own market-rate judgment.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group rebook the Hotel for another meeting within one (1) year of the cancellation, Hotel will credit 100% of the room revenue generated by that rebooking toward the damages owed, up to the amount of damages paid, without regard to the rate at which the rebooking occurs.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall forfeit the right to rebooking credit if the new event is booked at a rate materially lower than market rate for the applicable dates.

findings.finding_text: Force majeure clause matches CD's standard closely (illegal/impossible/impracticable, pandemic, travel advisories, unsafe-to-travel language, prompt deposit refund). One gap: it does not specify a refund timeframe as concrete as CD's 5-business-day standard, only 'promptly.'
findings.cd_standard: Deposits should be refunded within a defined window (CD standard: 5 business days).
findings.proposed_language: If this Agreement is terminated or substantially performed by reason of a force majeure event, any Deposits paid by Group shall be refunded within five (5) business days of the notice of termination.
findings.quoted_text: If this Agreement is terminated or substantially performed by reason of a force majeure event, any Deposits paid by Group shall be refunded promptly to Group.

findings.finding_text: Cutoff date of 30 days matches CD's range, and post-cutoff reservations remain available at group rate subject to availability, consistent with CD's standard. However, a footer note states the block is 'released in full' at the cutoff, which contradicts the body text's space-available continuation and could be read to eliminate group-rate access entirely after cutoff.
findings.cd_standard: Reservations after cutoff should remain available at group rate subject to availability, not automatically revert or release the block entirely.
findings.proposed_language: Clarify that after the cutoff date, the Hotel will continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis, and delete or reconcile the footer statement that the block is 'released in full' at cutoff, as it conflicts with Section 3.
findings.quoted_text: Reservations must be received no later than 30 days prior to arrival; the room block is released in full at that time.

findings.finding_text: Walk/relocation clause meets or exceeds CD's standard (comparable/superior hotel, transportation, upgrade, $50/night amenity, full pickup/commission credit). No material gap identified beyond noting the amenity is a dollar amount rather than the GM welcome amenity language, which is immaterial.
findings.cd_standard: Comparable or better accommodations, transportation, message forwarding, upgrade/welcome amenity, and pickup/commission credit with no attrition liability.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary; consider adding explicit message/mail-forwarding obligation for completeness.
findings.quoted_text: Upon the relocated Group member's return to Granite Bay Hotel and Spa, the guest shall be assigned an upgraded room category, complimentary for the returned nights, and shall receive a welcome amenity valued at not less than fifty dollars ($50.00) per night.

findings.finding_text: Mandatory fee disclosure clause matches CD's standard: full pre-signature disclosure required, undisclosed charges waived, no resort fee charged.
findings.cd_standard: All mandatory fees must be disclosed pre-signature; undisclosed charges waived.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: Any charge not disclosed in writing to Group before execution of this Agreement shall be waived in full and shall not be billed to Group or its attendees.

findings.finding_text: Complimentary room ratio of 1:40 matches CD's standard and credit survives attrition shortfalls, which is favorable to Group beyond CD's baseline.
findings.cd_standard: 1 comp room per 40 occupied room nights, cumulative, regardless of block performance.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall receive complimentary rooms based on a ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) paid rooms occupied during the event dates of April 26-29, 2027.

findings.finding_text: Assignment clause allows Group to assign to a successor/affiliated entity with Hotel consent not unreasonably withheld, consistent with CD standard.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign to successor/affiliate without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: The Group may assign this Agreement to a successor entity or affiliated management organization with written notice to the Hotel, provided that any such assignment shall not relieve the Group of its obligations hereunder and the assignee shall assume all duties and liabilities of the Group under this Agreement in writing.

findings.finding_text: Clause lacks the upfront representation that Hotel has no current renovation plans, gives only 14 days' notice (vs CD's 30), gives Group only 7 days to respond (vs CD's 30), and omits arbitration for disputed interference determinations. Also, notice is only required if the Hotel itself determines the work is material, giving Hotel discretion over whether notice is triggered at all.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should represent no current renovation plans, give 30 days' notice with scope/schedule/mitigation plan, allow Group to terminate without liability, and provide for arbitration on disputed interference.
findings.proposed_language: As of the date of this Agreement, Hotel has no plans for renovation or remodeling of any facilities to be used by Group, other than ordinary maintenance. If Hotel later confirms any such plans, Hotel will notify Group in writing within thirty (30) days, describing the scope, schedule, anticipated impact, and mitigation plan. Group may terminate without liability upon written notice given within thirty (30) days of receiving Hotel's notice. Disputes over interference will be resolved by binding arbitration before the event dates.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel makes no warranty, representation, or undertaking with respect to any construction, renovation, alteration, or other work that may be planned or under way at the Hotel during the event dates.

findings.finding_text: Finance charge on late undisputed balances is 2% per month compounded monthly — double CD's 1% cap and compounding rather than simple interest. Also, the dispute window is only 7 days (vs. CD's 30 days), and undisputed charges are 'deemed accepted' if not challenged within that short window, increasing risk that legitimate disputes are time-barred. Prepayment absent credit approval is 50% of anticipated charges, which is a defined percentage consistent with CD's standard, but the other billing terms deviate.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charge should be capped at 1% per month (not compounded) with a genuine dispute window (CD standard: 30 days) before any finance charge accrues on disputed amounts.
findings.proposed_language: Group will have thirty (30) days from receipt of each invoice to review and dispute any charge in good faith before any finance charge accrues on the disputed amount. Payment of undisputed charges is due within thirty (30) days of invoice date; any unpaid, undisputed balance will accrue a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, simple (not compounded), or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less.
findings.quoted_text: Any amounts not paid within thirty (30) days of the due date shall accrue a monthly finance charge of two percent (2%) per month on the outstanding balance, compounded monthly, until paid in full.
findings.exposure_basis: 2% compounded monthly finance charge vs CD's 1% simple cap; exact dollar exposure depends on unpaid balance duration, not calculable from contract alone.

findings.finding_text: The 7-day invoice dispute window is much shorter than CD's standard 30-day window, increasing risk that Group forfeits the right to challenge erroneous charges before they become final and binding.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have 30 days to dispute charges before they are deemed accepted.
findings.proposed_language: Group shall have thirty (30) days from receipt of each invoice to notify the Hotel in writing of any disputed charges; invoices not disputed within this thirty (30) day window shall be deemed accepted.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall have seven (7) days from receipt of each invoice to notify the Hotel in writing of any disputed charges; invoices not disputed within this seven (7) day window shall be deemed accepted by Group and shall be final and binding.

findings.finding_text: Reporting clause substantially matches CD's standard: weekly pickup reports starting 8 weeks prior, post-event report within 30 days, and no-cost audit rights. No material deviation identified.
findings.cd_standard: Weekly pickup reports, full post-event report within 30 days, no-cost audit rights.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: Beginning eight (8) weeks prior to the Event dates of April 26-29, 2027, the Hotel shall provide the Group with a written pickup report each week showing current room reservations, cancellations, and projected occupancy against the agreed room block.

findings.finding_text: Indemnification is mutual, limited to each party's own negligence/willful misconduct, and excludes indemnifying the other party's own negligence — consistent with CD's standard. Insurance requirement ($1M) is proportionate and standard.
findings.cd_standard: Mutual indemnification limited to own negligence; proportionate insurance requirements.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding the foregoing, each party's indemnity obligation shall be limited to losses and claims arising solely from such indemnifying party's own negligence or willful misconduct, and shall not extend to claims arising from the sole or comparative negligence of the indemnified party or any third party.

findings.finding_text: No security deposit is required, and damage charges are separately documented and not applied against attrition/F&B/cancellation obligations, consistent with CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Deposit should not be commingled with other charges like attrition or F&B minimums.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: Any damage charges recovered by the Hotel shall be applied solely to the documented repair and restoration of Hotel property and shall not be applied to any other charges, fees, or obligations owing by Group.

findings.finding_text: Termination for cause is separate from cancellation damages and provides refund, consistent with CD's standard, though the clause does not enumerate the specific triggering events (force majeure, labor dispute, brand change, renovation interference) as a consolidated list — those are instead addressed piecemeal in other sections. This is a structural note rather than a substantive gap since the underlying rights largely exist elsewhere in the contract.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should cover force majeure, labor dispute, ownership/brand change, and renovation interference in a no-liability, prompt-refund framework.
findings.proposed_language: Consider consolidating termination-for-cause triggers (force majeure, labor dispute, brand/ownership change, renovation interference) into Section 8 for clarity, though the substantive rights appear elsewhere in the Agreement.
findings.quoted_text: Termination for cause is a separate remedy and distinct from the cancellation damages provisions set forth in the cancellation clause.

findings.finding_text: Brand/ownership change clause matches CD's standard: 30-day notice, 30-day termination window. Missing explicit refund timeframe (CD standard: 5 business days) — refund terms not specified in this section for this trigger.
findings.cd_standard: Deposits should be refunded within 5 business days of termination notice.
findings.proposed_language: Add: Hotel will refund all deposits and prepayments made by Group within five (5) business days of Group's notice of termination under this clause.
findings.quoted_text: Upon receipt of notice of any change in brand, management, ownership, foreclosure, bankruptcy, or insolvency as described above, Group shall have thirty (30) days within which to terminate this Agreement without penalty or further obligation, provided that Group exercises such termination right by delivering written notice to the Hotel.
findings.location_section: 18. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership

findings.finding_text: Named storm clause is present and provides a 72-hour notice window with prompt refund, consistent with CD's standard, and improves on it by specifying a 50% probability threshold from NWS.
findings.cd_standard: Named storm clause with own notice period and cancellation window.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: If a named storm is forecast to strike the Hotel's location prior to or during the Event dates with a probability of occurrence of fifty percent (50%) or greater as determined by the National Weather Service or other authoritative meteorological source, either party may provide written notice of cancellation to the other party, provided such notice is delivered at least seventy-two (72) hours before the scheduled arrival of Group at the Hotel.

findings.finding_text: Attendee data clause exceeds CD's standard, prohibiting Hotel marketing use and third-party sharing without consent, with termination right for breach.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should not use rooming list/attendee data for its own marketing or share with third parties without consent.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not use any attendee data or personal information provided by the Group in connection with the Event for the Hotel's own marketing purposes or promotional activities.

findings.finding_text: ADA clause matches CD's standard on hotel warranty and cost allocation for auxiliary aids, though it does not explicitly state mutual indemnification limited to each party's own ADA obligations — instead framed only as a dispute-resolution/cost-allocation mechanism.
findings.cd_standard: Each party should indemnify the other only for its own ADA obligations, alongside the cost-allocation split.
findings.proposed_language: Add: Hotel and Group will each indemnify and hold harmless the other from liability arising from that party's own obligations under the ADA.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel represents and warrants that all guest rooms, public areas, and function space at Granite Bay Hotel and Spa are designed, maintained, and operated in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act and all applicable state and local accessibility laws.

findings.finding_text: Governing law/venue is Group's state, punitive damages excluded, and each party bears own fees — fully consistent with CD's standard.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law/venue should be Group's location, no punitive damages, each party bears own fees.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the state in which Group maintains its principal offices, without regard to its conflict of law principles.

findings.finding_text: Hotel explicitly disclaims any obligation to give advance notice of CBA expiration dates or labor disputes, contrary to CD's standard. Worse, even where Group can cancel for a labor disruption, the clause expressly states Group remains liable for ALL financial obligations (room charges, F&B minimums, other fees) despite cancellation — directly contradicting CD's standard of no liability at all in a labor-dispute cancellation.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should give advance notice of CBA expirations and labor disputes; Group should be able to cancel with NO liability if a strike/lockout/expired CBA arises within 90 days of the event.
findings.proposed_language: One year in advance, Hotel will provide Group in writing a list of all collective bargaining agreement expiration dates for the ensuing year, and will notify Group within ten (10) working days of becoming aware of any labor dispute. If, within ninety (90) days prior to or during the Event, Hotel's contract with its union employees has expired, or a strike, lockout, or picketing occurs, Group may cancel this Agreement by written notice without any liability whatsoever, including no liability for room charges, F&B minimums, or other fees, and any deposits or payments made by Group will be promptly refunded.
findings.quoted_text: Notwithstanding any such cancellation right, the occurrence of any labor dispute or labor-related disruption at the Hotel shall not relieve Group of any financial obligation, payment requirement, or other liability under this Agreement, including but not limited to room charges, food and beverage minimums, and any other fees or charges incurred by or on behalf of Group.
findings.exposure_basis: Group could be forced to cancel due to a labor dispute yet still remain liable for the full $155,000 F&B minimum (and room charges on 230 rooms x 4 nights x $372) despite not being at fault and not receiving the event it contracted for.

findings.finding_text: Rate parity clause meets or exceeds CD's standard: retroactive adjustment, no loss of commission/pickup credit/incentives.
findings.cd_standard: Rate should be adjusted retroactively without loss of commission or pickup credit.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: Group's eligibility for commissions, pickup credit, and other incentives shall not be diminished, reduced, or otherwise affected by any rate adjustment required under this clause.

findings.finding_text: Gratuity and service charge are conflated into a single undefined 25% charge, with the Hotel granted sole discretion to retain the entire amount as revenue rather than distributing any portion to staff who worked the event. This directly contradicts CD's standard requiring gratuity to be fully distributed to staff and service charge to be separately disclosed as hotel revenue.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity should be fully distributed to staff who worked the event; any separate service charge should be disclosed as hotel revenue, not conflated with gratuity.
findings.proposed_language: Any gratuity charged to Group's account will be fully distributed to the servers, bussers, and bartenders assigned to the Event. Any service charge is separate from gratuity, is not distributed as a tip, and is retained by Hotel to cover discretionary costs of the Event. Both charges and their respective percentages will be separately disclosed to Group in writing prior to the Event.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel retains sole discretion to determine the allocation and distribution of any gratuity collected on behalf of Group, and the Hotel may retain such gratuity as Hotel revenue without obligation to distribute it to service staff.
findings.exposure_basis: 25% service charge/gratuity on the $155,000 F&B minimum equals $38,750 that the Hotel may retain entirely as revenue with no obligation to pass any portion to staff who worked the event.

findings.finding_text: Resale/mitigation duty clause matches or exceeds CD's standard: diligent good-faith resale efforts, dollar-for-dollar credit, detailed accounting within 30 days, and inspection rights.
findings.cd_standard: Affirmative documented duty to resell, with proceeds credited and records available to verify effort.
findings.proposed_language: No change necessary.
findings.quoted_text: Any revenues realized from the resale of Guest Rooms and function space released by Group shall be credited dollar-for-dollar against the charges and fees otherwise due from Group under this Agreement, thereby reducing Group's financial obligation to the extent of such resale proceeds.

analysis.document_notes: The contract is well-organized with numbered sections closely mirroring standard industry clause categories, making comparison against the standards library straightforward. Notably, several clauses (attrition, force majeure, named storm, rate parity, complimentary rooms, resale mitigation, reporting/audit, mandatory fees) are drafted almost verbatim to CD's preferred fallback language and are favorable to Group. However, a small number of clauses contain significant, high-exposure deviations embedded within otherwise favorable-sounding language: the F&B shortfall formula is keyed to room revenue rather than the F&B gap itself, the gratuity/service charge provision conflates gratuity and service charge and permits full Hotel retention, the labor disputes clause preserves Group's full financial liability even when Group exercises its cancellation right due to a labor disruption, and the outside vendor clause imposes a mandatory exclusivity requirement with a flat surcharge. A footer notation ("room block is released in full" at cutoff) also appears to conflict with the body text of Section 3 regarding continued space-available access to the group rate after cutoff. These discrepancies warrant particular attention in negotiation despite the document's generally CD-aligned structure.

findings.finding_text: Attrition is measured night-by-night rather than cumulatively across the block, with an 85% threshold (vs. CD's 70% standard) and damages calculated at 70% of the nightly rate for each unoccupied room night below threshold. Night-by-night measurement dramatically increases exposure because strong nights cannot offset weak nights. There is also a contradictory two-table structure risk elsewhere in the contract (cancellation section) that suggests boilerplate inconsistency, but for attrition itself, the 85% trigger and per-night calculation are both unfavorable. Additionally, the clause imposes a 30-day deadline after which Group's failure to request records constitutes acceptance of Hotel's calculation, effectively cutting off audit rights.
findings.cd_standard: Attrition liability should be cumulative across the entire block, triggered only below 70% pickup, with full credit for any night hitting 95%+ occupancy and open-ended audit rights.
findings.proposed_language: Attrition liability, if any, will be calculated on a cumulative (not night-by-night) basis, with liability triggered only if Group's actual pickup falls below seventy percent (70%) of the total contracted room block. For each unsold room night below that threshold, Group will pay an amount equal to seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate (plus applicable tax). For any night the Hotel achieves 95% occupancy or higher, Group will receive full credit toward its block commitment for that night. Group's right to request and review occupancy records shall not be time-limited or waived by delay.
findings.quoted_text: Attrition is measured on a night-by-night basis and applies to the total room nights committed by Group under this Agreement.
findings.exposure_basis: Full block = 930 room nights (186 rooms x 5 nights). 85% threshold = 790.5 room nights required; below that, shortfall room nights x $279 x 70%. If pickup fell to 70% (CD standard trigger) instead of 85%, the additional room nights exposed to liability at the 85% vs 70% threshold difference = 15% of 930 = 139.5 room nights x $279 x 70% = ~$27,242 in additional exposure per this gap alone; total worst-case exposure if attrition falls to 0% pickup = 930 x $279 x 0.70 = $181,629, but night-by-night calculation could increase this further since strong nights don't offset weak ones.

findings.finding_text: Audit/records request right is subject to a 30-day post-event forfeiture clause, effectively waiving Group's right to dispute the Hotel's attrition calculation if not exercised promptly.
findings.cd_standard: Group should have unrestricted audit rights to verify attrition calculations.
findings.proposed_language: Group's right to request and review Hotel's occupancy records supporting any attrition calculation shall not expire and shall not be deemed waived by the passage of time.
findings.quoted_text: Group's failure to request occupancy records within thirty (30) days following the Event shall constitute acceptance of Hotel's attrition calculation.

findings.finding_text: The narrative cancellation damages schedule (20-80% sliding scale based on gross room revenue) conflicts directly with a separate table showing different percentages (23%-90%) also tied to days-prior-to-arrival brackets.
