This internal inconsistency creates ambiguity as to which schedule governs, and both schedules calculate damages against gross room revenue rather than room profit (70% of rate), inflating exposure. Additionally, resale credit only applies at 'original group rate' with no obligation to accept lower rates, and rebooking credit is discretionary rather than automatic.
findings.cd_standard: Cancellation damages should be based on room profit (70% of rate) on a sliding scale, with mandatory resale mitigation credited and automatic credit for rebooking within a reasonable window; the contract should not contain conflicting damage schedules.
findings.proposed_language: Liquidated damages will be calculated as a percentage of room profit — defined as seventy percent (70%) of the confirmed group room rate — on a sliding scale based on days prior to arrival, with no liability for cancellation twelve (12) months or more prior to arrival. Please resolve the discrepancy between the narrative damages schedule (20%-80%) and the table (23%-90%) so that only one, lower schedule governs. Hotel will use reasonable efforts to resell cancelled rooms at any rate reasonably obtainable, not solely the original group rate, and credit that revenue against damages. Should Group rebook the Hotel within one (1) year, 100% of the rebooking room revenue will automatically be credited toward damages owed.
findings.quoted_text: If notice is provided fewer than sixty (60) days before the Event start date, damages shall equal eighty percent (80%) of gross room revenue.
findings.exposure_basis: Gross room revenue = 930 room nights x $279 = $259,470. At worst-case 90% (per the conflicting table) = $233,523; at 80% (per narrative text) = $207,576. Using room profit standard (70% of rate) at 90% would be $163,466 instead — a gap of roughly $70,000-$186,000 in potential overcharge depending on which schedule and basis applies. Using the higher table figure of 90% of gross revenue as worst case: $259,470 x 0.90 = $233,523.

findings.finding_text: Rebooking with the Hotel earns no automatic credit against damages already owed — credit is applied only 'at Hotel's discretion' toward future room charges, not guaranteed against the damages themselves.
findings.cd_standard: Should Group rebook the Hotel within a reasonable window, 100% of the rebooking room revenue should be credited toward damages owed.
findings.proposed_language: Should Group rebook the Hotel for another meeting within one (1) year of cancellation, Hotel will credit 100% of the room revenue generated by that rebooking toward the damages owed, up to the amount of damages paid.
findings.quoted_text: Rebooking with the Hotel later earns Group no credit against damages already owed, provided that amounts paid as liquidated damages shall be applied as a credit against room charges for any future rebooking at Hotel at Hotel's discretion.

findings.finding_text: F&B shortfall is billed dollar-for-dollar (full difference) rather than a fraction of the gap. A separate paragraph purports to give Hotel additional discretionary power to renegotiate or apply 'additional event fees' if the shortfall exceeds 35% and is attributable to Group-initiated reductions — this is an added penalty layered on top of the full shortfall liability, not a cap.
findings.cd_standard: F&B shortfall should be billed at 35% of the gap, not dollar-for-dollar, and menu pricing should not be locked more than 12 months out.
findings.proposed_language: If actual food and beverage revenue is less than the $310,000 minimum, Group will pay Hotel thirty-five percent (35%) of the difference between actual revenue and the minimum, not the full shortfall. The Hotel's right to impose additional fees or renegotiate terms for shortfalls attributable to Group-initiated changes should be removed.
findings.quoted_text: Should the Group's actual food and beverage charges fall short of the Minimum F&B Commitment, the Group shall be obligated to pay the Hotel a shortfall fee equal to the difference between the Minimum F&B Commitment and the actual charges incurred.
findings.exposure_basis: Worst case (zero F&B revenue) exposure under dollar-for-dollar shortfall = full $310,000 minimum, versus $108,500 (35% of $310,000) under CD standard — a potential overexposure of up to $201,500.

findings.finding_text: Outside vendor clause matches CD standard — no surcharge, Group free to use vendor of choice for A/V, decorating, security, transportation.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be free to use outside vendors at no additional fee or surcharge.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not assess any charge, surcharge, or fee in connection with the Group's engagement of such outside vendors, and the outside vendor surcharge is expressly stated as $0.00.

findings.finding_text: Cutoff date is set at 40 days prior to arrival, longer than CD's preferred 21-30 day window, reducing the time Group has to fill the block and increasing attrition risk. Post-cutoff reservations are subject to Hotel's sole discretion to reassign block rooms to general inventory.
findings.cd_standard: Cutoff should be no earlier than 21-30 days prior to arrival, with group rate continuing space-available after cutoff.
findings.proposed_language: The cutoff date for the room block will be twenty-one (21) days prior to Group's arrival date. After the cutoff date, Hotel will continue to accept reservations at the group rate on a space-available basis.
findings.quoted_text: All reservations for rooms in the Group block must be requested and confirmed with Hotel no later than forty (40) days prior to the first date of the Event, which shall be August 2, 2027.

findings.finding_text: Walk clause provides comparable/superior accommodations and complimentary transportation but explicitly denies an upgrade or welcome amenity on return and denies pickup/commission credit for the relocated night, contrary to CD standard.
findings.cd_standard: Relocated nights should be credited toward Group's pickup and remain commissionable, and returning guests should receive an upgrade and welcome amenity.
findings.proposed_language: Upon the guest's return, Hotel will provide upgraded accommodations if available and a welcome amenity from the General Manager. Each displaced room will be credited toward Group's final pickup and remain commissionable, and will count toward any attrition/minimum calculation.
findings.quoted_text: the relocated guest shall return to the Vantage Point Hotel and Convention Center in a standard room assignment of the original booked category, with no room upgrade, no complimentary amenities beyond those included in the original rate agreement, and no additional services or concessions as compensation for the relocation. The relocated night or nights shall not be credited toward Group's room pickup for purposes of calculating minimum room guarantees, commission eligibility, or future rate negotiation under this Agreement or any successor agreement.

findings.finding_text: Despite an initial statement that undisclosed fees are waived, the clause simultaneously grants Hotel unilateral discretion to introduce new fees/surcharges after execution without prior notice, and to bind Group to them — directly contradicting the waiver language and CD's standard. A $26/night resort fee is disclosed, but the broader discretionary-fee language undermines protection.
findings.cd_standard: All mandatory fees must be disclosed in writing before signature; any undisclosed charge is waived, and Hotel should not have unilateral power to add new charges post-signature without Group's approval.
findings.proposed_language: Hotel may not introduce new fees, surcharges, or service charges after execution of this Agreement without Group's prior written approval. Any charge not disclosed in writing prior to signature is waived and may not be later imposed as a 'modification' to the fee schedule.
findings.quoted_text: Hotel may, at its sole discretion and without prior notice to Group, introduce additional fees, surcharges, and service charges after this Agreement is executed, and all such charges shall be binding upon Group as modifications to the schedule of fees set forth herein.
findings.exposure_basis: Unquantifiable open-ended exposure since new fees could be added at Hotel's sole discretion without cap or notice.

findings.finding_text: Complimentary room ratio matches CD's standard (1 per 40 paid rooms) and is protected from attrition-related forfeiture — favorable to Group.
findings.cd_standard: One complimentary room per 40 occupied room nights, calculated cumulatively, not forfeited due to attrition.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches or exceeds CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: Group shall receive complimentary room credit accruing at the ratio of one (1) complimentary room for every forty (40) paid rooms reserved and occupied by Group attendees during the Event Period of August 2-7, 2027.

findings.finding_text: Assignment clause allows assignment to successor/affiliated entities with Hotel consent not unreasonably withheld, consistent with CD standard, though it adds joint-and-several liability for Group post-assignment.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to assign to a successor management/affiliated entity without unreasonably withheld consent.
findings.proposed_language: No substantive change needed; note that joint-and-several liability post-assignment should be reviewed by Group's counsel for acceptability.
findings.quoted_text: Group may assign this Agreement to any direct successor entity or affiliated entity under common management control, including a parent company, subsidiary, or reorganized entity, provided that Group delivers written notice of such assignment to the Hotel at least thirty (30) days prior to the effective date of assignment, and the assignee assumes in writing all obligations of Group under this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Construction/renovation clause largely matches CD standard (no current plans warranty, 30-day notice, termination right) but lacks an arbitration mechanism for disputes about whether work interferes with the event, and gives Group only 7 days (vs no explicit CD minimum, but shorter window) to elect termination.
findings.cd_standard: Group should be able to terminate without liability if renovation interferes, with arbitration available if parties disagree.
findings.proposed_language: If the parties disagree whether the work will interfere with Group's event, the dispute will be resolved by binding arbitration before the event dates. Group's window to elect termination should be no less than thirty (30) days.
findings.quoted_text: Group may terminate this Agreement without liability or penalty upon written notice to the Hotel delivered within seven (7) days of receiving notice of the proposed work, provided that such termination must be delivered prior to the commencement of the Event.

findings.finding_text: Finance charge on late undisputed balances is set at 1.5% per month, compounded monthly, exceeding CD's 1% (or legal max, whichever is less) standard, and compounding increases the effective rate further.
findings.cd_standard: Finance charge on late, undisputed balances should be capped at 1% per month or legal maximum, whichever is less, not compounded.
findings.proposed_language: If payment of all undisputed charges is not received within thirty (30) days of invoice, a finance charge not to exceed one percent (1.0%) per month, or the maximum allowed by law, whichever is less, will apply to the unpaid, undisputed balance, without compounding.
findings.quoted_text: the Hotel shall assess a finance charge of 1.5% per month, or the maximum rate permitted by law, whichever is lower, calculated on the unpaid principal balance and compounded monthly until payment is received in full.

findings.finding_text: Reporting and audit clause meets or exceeds CD standard: weekly pickup reports beginning 12 weeks out, full post-event report within 30 days, and a no-cost audit right for Group. This is favorable.
findings.cd_standard: Weekly pickup reports, full post-event report within 30 days, no-cost audit right comparing guest lists.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches or exceeds CD standard, though it does not specify that miscoded rooms will be credited to Group's pickup regardless of rate paid — recommend adding that protection.
findings.quoted_text: Beginning twelve (12) weeks prior to the event and continuing weekly through the cutoff date established in the Event Order, the Hotel shall provide Group with a written pickup report detailing current room block reservations, cancellations, and room type distribution.

findings.finding_text: Indemnification is mutual and limited to each party's own negligence/willful misconduct, matching CD standard. Insurance requirement ($3M per occurrence/aggregate) appears proportionate but should be checked against actual event size/scope.
findings.cd_standard: Indemnification should be mutual, limited to each party's own negligence, with proportionate insurance requirements.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: each party's indemnity obligation shall be limited to losses and damages arising solely from that party's own negligence or willful misconduct, and neither party shall indemnify the other for any loss or damage arising from the other party's gross negligence, willful misconduct, or breach of law.

findings.finding_text: Security deposit ($30,000) is refundable within 45 days (slightly longer than CD's 30-day standard) and is properly restricted to documented damage only, not commingled with attrition/F&B shortfalls — largely favorable but refund window exceeds standard.
findings.cd_standard: Deposit should be refunded within 30 days absent documented damage, and not applied to unrelated charges.
findings.proposed_language: Any portion of the deposit not applied to documented damage claims shall be refunded to Group within thirty (30) days of Group's final checkout.
findings.quoted_text: Any portion of the deposit not applied to documented damage claims shall be refunded to Group within forty-five (45) days of Group's final checkout, provided all rooms have been inspected and the master account has been reconciled.

findings.finding_text: Termination-for-cause clause is one-sided: it grants only the Hotel the right to terminate immediately and without cause 'in its sole discretion' if it determines performance is impracticable, with no corresponding termination-for-cause right granted to Group for force majeure, labor disputes, brand change, or renovation collected in one place (those rights exist in separate clauses but are not cross-referenced here). The Hotel's unilateral, discretionary termination right is a one-way option that does not require an objective triggering event.
findings.cd_standard: Termination for cause should allow Group to walk away with no liability upon force majeure, labor dispute, brand/ownership change, or interfering renovation, with prompt refund, separate from cancellation damages.
findings.proposed_language: Termination for cause rights should be mutual and tied to objective triggering events (force majeure, labor dispute, brand/ownership change, interfering renovation) rather than the Hotel's unilateral, sole-discretion determination that performance is 'impracticable.' Group's rights under those other clauses should be cross-referenced here to confirm they are not superseded by this provision.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel may terminate this Agreement immediately and without cause upon written notice to the Group if the Hotel determines in its sole discretion that circumstances render performance impossible or commercially impracticable.

findings.finding_text: Brand/ownership change clause matches CD standard, including bankruptcy/foreclosure triggers and 30-day notice/termination window.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should notify Group within 30 days of brand/ownership/management change or bankruptcy/foreclosure, with Group able to terminate within 30 days without liability.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.
findings.location_section: 18. Change of Brand, Management or Ownership
findings.quoted_text: Upon receipt of notice of any such change, Group shall have a period of thirty (30) days within which to elect to terminate this Agreement without liability, penalty, or forfeiture of deposits or payments made to date.

findings.finding_text: Named storm clause is present with a defined trigger (landfall within 75 miles or within 72 hours of arrival) but the cancellation right expires 72 hours before opening day, which is a narrow window given named storms are typically tracked further in advance; also Seattle is an atypical market for hurricane risk, so the practical exposure is minimal, but the short window itself is a gap versus CD's broader standard.
findings.cd_standard: Named storm clause should allow cancellation without liability when a storm is forecast to affect the venue within a reasonable window before the event.
findings.proposed_language: In the event a named storm is forecast to affect the Hotel's location within 72 hours of any event date, Group may cancel the affected portion of the event without liability upon written or verbal (followed by written) notice, and this right shall not expire prematurely relative to the forecast timeline.
findings.quoted_text: Group's right to cancel on account of a named storm shall expire upon the expiration of seventy-two (72) hours before the Event's opening day; if no cancellation notice is received by the Hotel prior to the expiration of such window, Group shall have no further right to cancel on grounds of named storm and shall remain bound by all terms and conditions of this Agreement.

findings.finding_text: Attendee data clause fully matches and exceeds CD standard, with strong confidentiality, no marketing use, no third-party sale, and destruction/return obligations.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should not use rooming list/attendee data for its own marketing or sell to third parties without consent.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause exceeds CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall not use attendee data, including names, contact information, and registration details, for the Hotel's own marketing purposes or promotional activities.

findings.finding_text: ADA clause matches CD standard, warranting compliance and dividing auxiliary aid costs by area of responsibility (Hotel facilities vs. Group program content).
findings.cd_standard: Hotel should warrant ADA compliance and divide auxiliary aid funding between Group (event space) and Hotel (guest rooms/common areas).
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel shall be responsible for auxiliary aids that relate to the Hotel's facilities and operations, and the Group shall be responsible for auxiliary aids that relate to the Group's program content and services.

findings.finding_text: Governing law/venue clause matches CD standard: uses Group's home state, no punitive damages, each party bears own attorney's fees.
findings.cd_standard: Governing law/venue should be Group's location, no punitive damages, each party bears own fees.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: This Agreement and all matters arising from or relating to it shall be governed by the laws of the state in which Group maintains its principal offices, without regard to any conflicts of law principles or the law of any other jurisdiction.

findings.finding_text: Labor disputes clause largely matches CD standard (12-month CBA expiration notice, 90-day cancellation window) but adds a carve-out limiting Group's cancellation right if Hotel unilaterally determines the dispute is 'resolved to the satisfaction of Group' and that 'full Hotel services will be available' — this gives Hotel a subjective escape hatch not present in CD's standard, which calls for an unconditional right to cancel regardless of whether Hotel can still perform.
findings.cd_standard: If a strike/lockout/expired CBA arises within 90 days of the event, Group should be able to cancel with no liability regardless of whether Hotel can technically still perform.
findings.proposed_language: Group's right to cancel without liability under this clause shall not be conditioned on the Hotel's determination that the dispute has been resolved or that services will be available; the right shall apply regardless of whether Hotel is able to perform.
findings.quoted_text: Group's right to cancel without liability under this clause shall not apply if the labor dispute is resolved to the satisfaction of Group and the Hotel determines that full Hotel services will be available for the Event dates, and Group shall have had a reasonable opportunity to assess the impact of any labor action.

findings.finding_text: Rate parity clause guarantees no lower public rate during event dates and preserves commission/pickup credit, but the rate adjustment for violations applies only prospectively to new reservations, not retroactively to reservations already confirmed prior to discovery of the lower rate — contrary to CD standard requiring retroactive adjustment.
findings.cd_standard: If Hotel breaches rate parity, Group's rate should be adjusted to match, including retroactively for reservations already made.
findings.proposed_language: If Hotel offers a lower guestroom rate, Hotel will adjust the rate for all prior reservations in Group's block to match, retroactively, and make the adjusted rate available to all Group attendees.
findings.quoted_text: Any rate adjustment or modification resulting from such discovery shall apply only to reservations made after the lower rate is identified and communicated to Group in writing, and shall not apply retroactively to any reservations confirmed prior to such identification.

findings.finding_text: Gratuity/service charge clause matches CD standard: gratuity fully distributed to staff, service charge (22%) clearly disclosed as separate Hotel revenue, not represented as a tip.
findings.cd_standard: Gratuity and service charge should be clearly and separately defined and disclosed.
findings.proposed_language: No change needed; clause matches CD standard.
findings.quoted_text: The service charge imposed under this Agreement represents the Hotel's revenue and compensation for administrative, planning, and operational services and shall not be characterized, represented, or construed as a tip, gratuity, or compensation to service staff.

findings.finding_text: The resale of released inventory clause explicitly exempts the Hotel's resale efforts, records, and documentation from any audit, disclosure, or review by Group — directly contrary to CD standard requiring records be made available to verify mitigation efforts actually happened. This undermines Group's ability to verify resale credits are being properly applied against damages.
findings.cd_standard: Hotel's resale/mitigation records should be available to Group upon request to verify the effort actually happened.
findings.proposed_language: Call reports, sales logs, and actual occupancy records documenting Hotel's resale/mitigation efforts will be made available to Group upon request to verify that net proceeds have been properly credited against Group's obligations.
findings.quoted_text: The Hotel's resale efforts, including any attempts to place canceled rooms or space, its marketing activities, pricing decisions, and all related records and documentation shall remain the sole property and responsibility of the Hotel and shall not be subject to disclosure to Group, audit by Group, or review by Group's representatives.

findings.finding_text: Force majeure clause requires that performance be rendered 'physically impossible' rather than merely impracticable, which is a materially higher bar than CD's standard (illegal, impossible, OR commercially impracticable). It does include pandemics and travel restrictions, which is favorable, but explicitly excludes attendee safety concerns or reluctance to travel absent an actual governmental order — narrower than CD's standard, which includes circumstances making it 'unsafe or imprudent' to travel even without a formal government mandate. Refund is also reduced by Hotel's 'documented costs incurred... specifically attributable to preparation,' an offset not contemplated by CD standard.
findings.cd_standard: Force majeure should excuse performance when illegal, impossible, or commercially impracticable, including when it is unsafe or imprudent for attendees to travel, without requiring a strict physical-impossibility standard, and deposits should be refunded promptly without cost offsets.
findings.proposed_language: Either party may cancel this Agreement without liability if performance is rendered illegal, impossible, or commercially impracticable, including circumstances that make it unsafe, illegal, or imprudent for attendees to travel to or assemble at the Hotel, regardless of whether a specific government order is directed at the Hotel's or attendees' location.
